raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Documentation for the v26.9 training images:

- `rocm/primus:v26.9` (Megatron-LM, TorchTitan, Megatron Bridge), built 2026-10-30
- `rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.9` (MaxText), built 2026-10-30

Both are built from Primus `db1a4160` on `release/v26.9`. The docs were written from the CI images that passed
QA, each probed under its release tag, with the release-docs-update skill.

**Stacked on #1374**, whose tools generated it: this PR targets `dev/release-docs-ci-images` and contains only
the 7 docs commits. It moves to `main` once #1374 is merged.

## Commits (one per phase)

1. **Image snapshots and release Dockerfiles**: `tools/release_docs/data/v26.9-{primus,jax}.json` and
   `.github/workflows/docker-release/Dockerfile.{primus,jax}-v26.9`, both taken from the images (the
   committed Dockerfiles match the images' baked-in copies).
2. **Version references** v26.8 → v26.9 across the docs, `README.md`, `runner/` and `primus/__init__.py`.
   References outside the documentation surface are kept: CI base images, example configs and their comments,
   tests, `tools/perf`.
3. **Release notes**: the v26.9 section (tables generated from the snapshots, the "Changes since v26.8" delta,
   Primus source) and the v26.9 Highlights for both families. The v26.8 Highlights move into the v26.8
   section; v26.6 leaves the detailed list.
4. **Recipe notes and new models**: "Important notes for v26.9" on the Megatron-LM, TorchTitan and MaxText
   pages, and the new recipes in the model lists and the model-support matrix (GLM-5.3-Flash,
   HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training, ZAYA1-8B FP8, MI325X ZAYA1-8B).
5. **Bare-metal install** re-pinned to the v26.9 Dockerfiles: `tools/installation*/setup.sh`, `env.sh`, the
   READMEs and the bare-metal guides.
6. **Review answers**: the JAX page no longer says the image ships no Primus (v26.9 bundles it again); history
   references restored to v26.8; the "Primus source" section notes that `release/v26.9` has moved past the
   build commit (`93dd9201`, MI325X GPT-OSS-20B and ZAYA1-8B tuning, #1355).
7. **Review edits**: the README "What's New" entry for v26.9, and a "Primus training performance" section in
   the overview linking AMD's published training results.

## Release highlights

**`rocm/primus:v26.9`**: a ROCm 10.2 nightly with a PyTorch 2.16 pre-release and a TransformerEngine 2.20
development build; new models (GLM-5.3-Flash, HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training, ZAYA1-8B FP8); a fused AdamW
optimizer by default in TorchTitan; MoE correctness fixes; mock-data benchmarks now use each model's real
vocabulary.

**`rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.9`**: JAX 0.12.0 and a TransformerEngine 2.19 development build on a ROCm 10.3
nightly; MaxText pinned to `release/v26.9`; Primus bundled in the image again; a lower default XLA autotuning
level fixes intermittent compile-time crashes.

Details and PR links are in `docs/01-getting-started/release-notes.md` under "Highlights for v26.9".

## Checks

- `release_notes.py check`: 123 values verified across all 6 documented images.
- `check_links.py` and `install_parity.py --check` pass.
- Bare-metal install and a 10-step training run of the v26.9 stacks passed on MI300X and MI355X for both
  families, from the same images, with the install scripts of #1374. They were not re-run on this exact branch.

## After merge

- Cherry-pick these commits to `release/v26.9`.
- Publish `rocm/primus:v26.9` and `rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.9`. The release notes already name these tags
  and their image IDs.

nodes.body: @peterjunpark This is the PR to update the Primus docs to v26.9. Please review it. Thank you

Follow-up on the PR Pundit review, addressed in 7263d1b3:

Fixed
- 1: the "Verifying the stack in an image" commands now use rocm/primus:v26.9.
- 2: the installation README now treats apex as the exception to the same-ROCm pin rule.
- 10: the MaxText profiling tag example is now v26.9_llama2_7b.
- 11: the README pip-install examples now use v26.9.0 / 26.9.0.
- 14: restored release/v26.8 as the MaxText release that made the TF extras opt-in.
- 15: linked #1286 for the TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 default.
- 16: reworded the flydsl pin note.

Not addressed in this PR
- 3, 8, 9, 17: these are comments in Dockerfile.*-v26.9, which are recorded copies of the Dockerfiles that built the release images, so they stay as built. Fixes belong in the CI source Dockerfiles.
- 5: this would change the image build, so it's out of scope for a docs PR.
- 4: this is a limitation of install_parity.py that predates this PR. It's a follow-up for the tool.
- 6, 7, 12: Pundit's own verification already found these don't apply.
- 13: this is a refactor of setup.sh with no user-facing effect.

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: Image verification commands pull and inspect v26.8: this PR left both `docker run` tags un-bumped
`docs/01-getting-started/release-notes.md:636`

Both `docker run` commands in 'Verifying the stack in an image' (lines 636 and 642) still use `rocm/primus:v26.8`, while every other current-image tag was bumped to v26.9. Users copying these commands inspect the previous release's image. Bump both to `rocm/primus:v26.9`.

**Who is affected:** Users following the 'Verifying the stack in an image' section of the v26.9 release notes.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

<details><summary>Nits and less certain findings (12)</summary>

**6. JAX TE wheel built for ROCm 10.2 nightly runs on a ROCm 10.3 image, risking ABI breakage** (`.github/workflows/docker-release/Dockerfile.jax-v26.9:260`)

`TE_VERSION=2.19.0.dev0+rocm10.2.0a20261002` sits on `THE_ROCK_VERSION=10.3.0a20261026`, with JAX plugins on rocm10.3.0a20261026, yet the release notes say TE is built against the image's nightly. The bare-metal script reproduces the mismatch, and the README's same-ROCm-build rule was weakened. This is a cross-nightly ABI risk: document it as a deliberate divergence or align the builds.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: head release-notes.md:148 says TE 2.19.0.dev0 is tagged rocm10.2.0a20261002 while the image's ROCm and JAX plugins are 10.3.0a20261026; the 'built against that nightly' sentence is in the v26.8 section (:342), where it was true. tools/installation-jax/README.md likewise says the TE pairing 'is the image's, and it is kept', so the divergence is already documented as the candidate asks._

**7. Validation headings claim v26.8 runtime validation while scripts install unvalidated v26.9 nightly pins** (`tools/installation/README.md:274`)

`tools/installation/README.md:274`, `tools/installation-jax/README.md:212` and the guides still say 'Runtime-validated for v26.8', but the scripts now install untested v26.9 nightly pins (ROCm 10.2 nightly, torch 2.16 pre-release, apex for ROCm 10.3). The README itself says 'The v26.9 pins have not been through a bare-metal run yet', so the 'deliberate, tested deviation' wording is no longer backed. Mark the v26.9 pins as unvalidated in these headings.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: Each 'Runtime-validated for v26.8' caveat already says 'The v26.9 pins have not been through a bare-metal run yet': tools/installation/README.md:274-282, tools/installation-jax/README.md:212-218, bare-metal-installation.md:632 and bare-metal-installation-jax.md:286. The quoted 'deliberate, tested deviation' sentence (README.md:219) is about Primus-Turbo's --no-deps install, not the validation heading, and was already on the base at line 228._

**8. `--reinstall` comment cites pip 26.2.1 and omits urllib3 CVEs while the stage builds 26.2.2** (`.github/workflows/docker-release/Dockerfile.primus-v26.9:137`)

The comment justifying `--reinstall` says the re-vendored wheel 'shares the 26.2.1 version string', but `ARG PIP_VERSION=26.2.2`; the same stale text is in `Dockerfile.jax-v26.9:167`. Reword it to reference `${PIP_VERSION}`. The adjacent comment also lists only the msgpack/setuptools IDs and omits the urllib3 CVEs that pip_builder now re-vendors.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers reading the v26.9 release Dockerfiles; the image build is unaffected.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**9. Datasets cap comment cites `pyarrow==21.0.0`, but the image force-installs `pyarrow==23.0.1`** (`.github/workflows/docker-release/Dockerfile.primus-v26.9:200`)

The new comment says `datasets` stays at 5.0.1 because 'Primus pins pyarrow==21.0.0'. That pin is real (`requirements.txt:24`), but this image overrides it with `pyarrow==23.0.1` (line 623). The release snapshot records 23.0.1. The cap is still correct, because 23.0.1 is also below the `pyarrow>=24` that `datasets` 5.1.0 needs. Cite the pyarrow version the image actually installs.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers reading the v26.9 primus Dockerfile when bumping datasets or pyarrow.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**10. Profiling example pairs `maxtext-v26.9` image with `v26.8_llama2_7b` tag: this PR bumped only `IMAGE`** (`docs/02-user-guide/jax-maxtext-training.md:425`)

The neighbouring IMAGE line now says maxtext-v26.9, but the TAG example still reads 'e.g. v26.8_llama2_7b'. Bump it to v26.9 so the paired example is consistent.

**Who is affected:** Readers copying the standalone Docker profiling example in the MaxText guide.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**11. README pip-install section installs Primus 26.2.0rc1 while Quick Start pins 26.9.0** (`README.md:83`)

The 'Install as a Python package' section of `README.md` still shows `git+...Primus.git@v26.2.0rc1` and `primus==26.2.0rc1` (lines 83, 86), while the Quick Start pip line now pins `primus==26.9.0`. This stale example predates this PR: the base already had `26.2.0rc1` there alongside `26.8.0`. Consider bumping both to `v26.9.0`/`26.9.0` while the release docs are being updated.

**Origin:** pre-existing

**Who is affected:** Readers who copy the pip-install example from the README get an old release candidate instead of v26.9.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**12. v26.9 MaxText notes still tell users to drop `pure_nnx_decoder`, an issue fixed in v26.8** (`docs/02-user-guide/jax-maxtext-training.md:37`)

'Important notes for v26.9' still includes 'Drop `pure_nnx_decoder` from local configs', which was fixed in v26.8 (#1228). The stale note sits next to the real v26.9 `retry_when_tokens_dropped` note and dilutes it. Remove it.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: In head docs/02-user-guide/jax-maxtext-training.md the note sits under the explicit sub-heading 'If you are moving from v26.7 or earlier:', separate from the v26.9 notes. It is guidance for users upgrading across v26.8, where the key was removed, not a stale v26.9 known issue._

**Related past reviews:** [#1052](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1052) on `docs/02-user-guide/jax-maxtext-training.md`

**13. Site-packages lookup heredoc now copied in four patch helpers: this PR added two more copies** (`tools/installation/setup.sh:361`)

New `patch_torch_cpp_extension` and `patch_fla_autotune_key` each copy the same 8-line Python heredoc that scans `sysconfig` purelib/platlib, giving four copies with `patch_apex_cxx20` and `patch_te_ck_jit` (lines 343, 364, 438, 825). Extract a single `site_file <relpath>` helper and call it from each patch function.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers of `tools/installation/setup.sh`; no runtime effect.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**14. JAX setup comment and guide claim MaxText `release/v26.9` made extras opt-in; v26.8 did** (`tools/installation-jax/setup.sh:335`)

The comment 'release/v26.8 made the TensorFlow, TFDS, seqio and JetStream extras opt-in' was mechanically changed to 'release/v26.9', which misstates when the change happened. Restore v26.8, e.g. 'Since release/v26.8 the ... extras are opt-in'.

**Who is affected:** Readers of the bare-metal JAX installer script and its guide.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**15. New `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` default explained only as 'memory issues', with no removal condition** (`tools/installation/env.sh:164`)

The new default is explained only as 'alongside Primus #1286, to resolve memory issues' in `env.sh`, `bare-metal-installation.md`, the installation README and `Dockerfile.primus-v26.9`. None say what the flag disables, what symptom it avoids, or when it can be removed. State the code path and symptom, link the issue, and give a removal condition.

**Who is affected:** Bare-metal users and maintainers who need to know why `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` is set and when to remove it.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**16. Readers can't tell what 'It is restated' refers to: this PR deleted the flydsl-pin antecedent** (`tools/installation/README.md:246`)

The edit removed 'Primus-Turbo itself now pins `flydsl==…`', leaving 'It is restated because Turbo is installed with `--no-deps`' with nothing to refer to. Rephrase it, e.g. 'Primus-Turbo declares this flydsl pin itself, but Turbo is installed with `--no-deps`, so `stage_turbo` restates it.'

**Who is affected:** Readers of `tools/installation/README.md` (the bare-metal install guide).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**17. Comgr workaround comment describes a same-RUN hardlink while code creates a symlink in another RUN** (`.github/workflows/docker-release/Dockerfile.primus-v26.9:250`)

The comment says the `ln -f` must share a RUN with the pip install to avoid overlayfs copy-up, but the code is `ln -sf` (a symlink) in the separate `rocm-sdk init` RUN, so the inode argument doesn't apply. The same text is in `Dockerfile.jax-v26.9`. Reword the comment to describe the symlink replacement.

**Origin:** pre-existing

**Who is affected:** Maintainers reading the comgr workaround in the new v26.9 Dockerfiles; the image builds the same either way.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

</details>

**2. 🟠 Should fix: Installation README says apex must match torch's ROCm, contradicting the new ROCm 10.3 apex pin**

The 'Index contents move' caveat in `tools/installation/README.md` (~line 292) still says `apex` must target the same ROCm version as `torch`/`rocm-sdk-*`. That contradicts the new pin `APEX_VERSION=1.16.0a0+rocm10.3.0a20261029` next to the 10.2.0a20261020 set. The same README (line 89) and `setup.sh` already explain that this is the build the v26.9 image itself resolved. Drop `apex` from that list and note it as the image's exception, as the PR already does in the other doc that carries this caveat.

**Who is affected:** Bare-metal installers who update the setup.sh pin block after a pin stops resolving.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**3. 🟠 Should fix: JAX image's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` comment describes TE 2.17, `jax_rocm7_plugin` and a nonexistent RCCL override**

The comment above `ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=""` was copied unchanged from the v26.7/v26.8 Dockerfiles. It still names 'TE 2.17', `jax_rocm7_plugin` and an 'in-place RCCL override in jax_base'. This image installs TE `2.19.0.dev0` and the `jax_rocm10_{pjrt,plugin}` 0.12.0 wheels, and has no in-place RCCL override. The ENV also sits before the JAX/TE installs, not 'after every build step'. Update the comment; it does not change the built image.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers debugging the double-ROCm-runtime segfault in the v26.9 JAX image.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

@@ -0,0 +1,629 @@
+ARG DEFAULT_BASE=ubuntu:24.04
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
+
+# uv: used as the installer for everything going into /opt/venv in jax_base
+# (faster resolves/installs than pip for this image's large ROCm/JAX/TE/torch
+# wheel sets). Pulled as a static binary from Astral's distroless image rather
+# than via pip. Needs its own named stage (rather than an ARG-interpolated
+# `COPY --from=` reference) since BuildKit doesn't support variable expansion
+# directly in --from.
+ARG UV_VERSION=0.12.7
+FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv_bin
+
+# rocm-sdk init (below) extracts a prebuilt bazelisk binary to /usr/local/bin/bazel
+# so ROCm/TheRock components can be rebuilt from source. That prebuilt binary is
+# stale (Go 1.23.0 stdlib, ~16 CVEs) and no newer official bazelisk release fixes
+# it either (still built with go1.24.0). Rebuild the same upstream source with a
+# current Go toolchain instead, preserving identical launcher behavior.
+FROM golang:1.26-bookworm AS bazelisk_builder
+ARG BAZELISK_VERSION=v1.29.0
+# bazelisk's own go.mod pins golang.org/x/crypto, golang.org/x/sys and
+# golang.org/x/net versions with known CVEs; bump them explicitly since no newer
+# bazelisk tag fixes this upstream. x/crypto uses a `replace` directive, not just
+# `go get`: as an indirect dep its require floor gets pulled back below the fix by
+# `go mod tidy`/MVS (observed drift to v0.54.0), while replace pins the build to
+# exactly v0.55.0. x/net is pinned exact (not -u) for the same drift reason.
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${BAZELISK_VERSION} https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazelisk.git /src \
+    && cd /src \
+    && go get -u golang.org/x/sys \
+    && go get golang.org/x/net@v0.56.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/crypto=golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 \
+    && go mod tidy \
+    && go build -o /bazelisk
+
+# transformer_engine_rocm_jax's own build vendors a copy of GoogleCloudPlatform/gcsfuse
+# (built to /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse) whose go.mod pins golang.org/x/text,
+# golang.org/x/net and google.golang.org/grpc versions with known CVEs; this isn't
+# fixed upstream as of gcsfuse's latest release, so rebuild the same binaries here
+# with those deps bumped and overwrite whatever TE's build (and later, MaxText's
+# apt-installed gcsfuse package) produced, preserving identical behavior. Both the
+# main gcsfuse binary and the mount.gcsfuse helper embed these deps, so both are
+# rebuilt. x/crypto and grpc use `replace` directives to force the CVE-fixed
+# versions past gcsfuse's own go.mod pins.
+FROM golang:1.26-bookworm AS gcsfuse_builder
+ARG GCSFUSE_VERSION=v3.11.2
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${GCSFUSE_VERSION} https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcsfuse.git /src \
+    && cd /src \
+    && go get golang.org/x/text@v0.39.0 \
+    && go get golang.org/x/net@v0.60.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace google.golang.org/grpc=google.golang.org/grpc@v1.83.2 \
+    && go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/crypto=golang.org/x/crypto@v0.57.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4=github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4@v4.1.6 \
+    && go mod tidy \
+    && go build -o /mount.gcsfuse ./tools/mount_gcsfuse \
+    && go build -o /gcsfuse .
+
+# pip's vendored msgpack, setuptools and urllib3 are flagged by Trivy via pip's SBOM
+# (pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json): GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964, CVE-2025-47273, CVE-2026-97687/97689.
+# Rebuild pip with msgpack 1.2.3, urllib3 2.8.0 and setuptools 79.0.1 (highest that
+# satisfies pip's `setuptools<80` vendor pin) so the regenerated SBOM is clean.
+FROM python:3.12-slim AS pip_builder
+ARG PIP_VERSION=26.2.2
+# build-essential: msgpack has no pure "any" wheel, so `vendoring sync` builds it
+# from sdist and needs a C compiler; the compiled .so is dropped afterward per
+# pip's own vendoring config, leaving the pure-Python copy pip ships.
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git build-essential \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && pip install vendoring build
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${PIP_VERSION} https://github.com/pypa/pip.git /src
+WORKDIR /src
+RUN sed -i \
+        -e 's/^msgpack==.*/msgpack==1.2.3/' \
+        -e 's/^setuptools==.*/setuptools==79.0.1/' \
+        -e 's/^\( *\)urllib3==.*/\1urllib3==2.8.0/' \
+        src/pip/_vendor/vendor.txt

**4. 🟠 Should fix: Parity `--check` reports torchvision/torchaudio drift as OK: this PR files identical pins as documented divergences**

`TORCHVISION_VERSION` and `TORCHAUDIO_VERSION` are now described in `documented_divergences.primus` as inline pins of the same version, not divergences. `compare()` puts any documented name with no Dockerfile counterpart into the divergent bucket without comparing values, so future drift on these pins would be reported as deliberate. The torchaudio entry, the empty `inline_pins.primus` and the `_comment` citing `Dockerfile.primus-v26.6` were already like this on the base. The torchvision entry is the one this PR changed from a real divergence. Moving them to `inline_pins` only helps if `${THE_ROCK_VERSION}` is substituted or the pattern captures only the literal part of the version: `inline_pins()` returns the raw capture, which would then show false drift against the script's literal value.

**Who is affected:** Release maintainers relying on `install_parity.py --check` to catch torch companion-wheel drift between `Dockerfile.primus-v26.9` and `tools/installation/setup.sh`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**5. 🟠 Should fix: JAX image build fetches full clones of unused PyTorch submodules: this PR restored `--recurse-submodules` clone**

The Primus layer in `Dockerfile.jax-v26.9` runs `git clone --recurse-submodules`. That fetches full, non-shallow clones of all 10 submodules in `.gitmodules` at the default-branch pins, before `git checkout ${PRIMUS_BRANCH}`. The layer then re-initialises only `third_party/maxtext`. The image uses its own `/workspace/maxtext` through `MAXTEXT_PATH`, so the PyTorch-backend submodules (Megatron-LM, torchtitan, Megatron-Bridge, Automodel, ...) are dead weight that costs build time and image size. The block is copied unchanged from `Dockerfile.jax-v26.4` through `v26.7`. A plain clone followed by a shallow `git submodule update --init --depth 1 third_party/maxtext` would avoid the cost.

**Who is affected:** Anyone building the v26.9 JAX release image; it costs build time and image size, and the image still works.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

+ARG TE_VERSION=2.19.0.dev0+rocm10.2.0a20261002.bfe94fb
+
+# flaxlib_src (bundled inside the flax wheel) is inert vendored Rust/C++ reference
+# source: flax only imports the compiled flaxlib extension when flax_use_flaxlib is
+# enabled (default off), and no such extension is ever built here, so it's unreachable
+# either way. Delete it below to drop its Cargo.lock (stale pyo3 CVE) with no behavior
+# change. This pin/deletion is repeated again after the Primus install further down,
+# since Primus transitively pulls in a newer flax that reintroduces flaxlib_src.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        pybind11==3.0.4 \
+        importlib-metadata==8.7.1 \
+        pydantic==2.13.4 \
+        flax==0.12.10 \
+    && uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://rocm.frameworks-nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch-staging/ \
+        --pre \
+        --no-build-isolation \
+        transformer_engine_rocm_jax==${TE_VERSION} \
+        transformer-engine-rocm10==${TE_VERSION} \
+    && sed -i 's|transformer-engine-rocm7|transformer-engine-rocm7", "transformer-engine-rocm10|g' \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformer_engine/common/__init__.py \
+    && find /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/orbax -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && rm -rf /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flaxlib_src \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+COPY --from=gcsfuse_builder /mount.gcsfuse /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse
+
+FROM jax_base AS jax_training
+
+# Intentionally root (no USER instruction): training entrypoints need direct
+# access to /dev/kfd and /dev/dri GPU device nodes and to AINIC/RDMA devices,
+# which a non-root user cannot reliably get across the container runtimes this
+# image is deployed on. Trivy DS-0002 is expected to keep flagging this;
+# tracked as an accepted risk rather than remediated here.
+
+# Configure required envs
+ENV NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=1
+ENV NVTE_USE_HIPBLASLT=1
+ENV GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+ENV HSA_FORCE_FINE_GRAIN_PCIE=1
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
+ENV NCCL_DEBUG=VERSION
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_BWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_FWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_IS_V3_ATOMIC_FP32=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_HOW_V3_BF16_CVT=2
+ENV XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=.9
+ENV XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor=95 --xla_gpu_reduce_scatter_combine_threshold_bytes=8589934592 --xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler=True --xla_gpu_all_gather_combine_threshold_bytes=8589934592 --xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=False --xla_gpu_enable_cublaslt=True --xla_gpu_autotune_level=0 --xla_gpu_enable_all_gather_combine_by_dim=FALSE --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=''"
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Install maxtext
+ARG MAXTEXT_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/maxtext.git
+ARG MAXTEXT_BRANCH=release/v26.9
+
+RUN git clone ${MAXTEXT_REPO} \
+    && cd maxtext \
+    && git checkout ${MAXTEXT_BRANCH} \
+    && chmod +x src/dependencies/scripts/setup.sh \
+    && ./src/dependencies/scripts/setup.sh TF=true \
+    && cd .. \
+    && find maxtext -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Make the clone above the one MaxText-consuming tools resolve to. Primus picks its
+# MaxText backend from MAXTEXT_PATH and otherwise falls back to its own
+# third_party/maxtext submodule, which pins whatever release Primus/main tracks
+# rather than MAXTEXT_BRANCH -- so without this a run silently tests the wrong
+# MaxText. Set as ENV (not just in the CI scripts) so every entrypoint in the image
+# inherits it. Primus's own bare-metal installer exports the same var for this reason
+# (Primus tools/installation-jax/env.sh).
+ENV MAXTEXT_PATH=/workspace/maxtext
+
+# Fix (root cause): the prebuilt PyPI TensorFlow wheel bundles an LLVM whose symbols
+# collide with ROCm 7.14's libLLVM inside Grain "spawn" workers -> SIGSEGV on
+# `import tensorflow` after `import jax`. Rebuild the CPU-only TF wheel from ROCm's
+# fork (correct symbol visibility) and install it in place of the stock wheel. A CPU
+# build also has no bundled NCCL, so it preserves the previous XLA-RCCL fix.
+# NOTE: bumps TF to 2.21.0 and adds a long (~30-60 min) bazel build to the image.
+# bazel is already installed via the bazelisk_builder stage above (jax_base ->
+# jax_training inherits /usr/local/bin/bazel) -- reused here rather than
+# re-downloading the vulnerable prebuilt bazelisk release.
+ARG TF_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/tensorflow-upstream.git
+ARG TF_BRANCH=upstream-v2.21.0
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip zip \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+# GitHub's on-the-fly gzip for the pinned LLVM archive has an unstable checksum that breaks
+# the TF build. Pull a frozen copy from our ACR and feed Bazel via --distdir (no network fetch).
+COPY --from=unifiedtrainingdockers.azurecr.io/utd/mirror:llvm-909041e4802c4b9a2223ca04099f35bf1dbbd460 \
+    /909041e4802c4b9a2223ca04099f35bf1dbbd460.tar.gz /opt/bazel_distdir/
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${TF_BRANCH} ${TF_REPO} tensorflow-upstream \
+    && cd tensorflow-upstream \
+    && grep -q 3f986184ee126677dbd77edb16d6b82c057ec869fefd7a9871979941e52e837a \
+        third_party/xla/third_party/llvm/workspace.bzl \
+    && bazel build //tensorflow/tools/pip_package:wheel \
+        --distdir=/opt/bazel_distdir \
+        --repo_env=WHEEL_NAME=tensorflow_cpu \
+        --repo_env=HERMETIC_PYTHON_VERSION=3.12 \
+    && uv pip uninstall tensorflow tensorflow-cpu tensorflow_cpu \
+    && uv pip install --no-deps \
+        bazel-bin/tensorflow/tools/pip_package/wheel_house/tensorflow_cpu-2.21.0-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf tensorflow-upstream /root/.cache/bazel /root/.cache /opt/bazel_distdir
+
+# Primus
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus.git
+# Latest commit on `release/v26.9` branch. Commited on 2026-10-30.
+ARG PRIMUS_BRANCH=db1a41601833294231daadb3cdbb2933eb805c73
+
+RUN git clone --recurse-submodules ${PRIMUS_REPO} \

@@ -15,25 +15,234 @@ Every version below was read out of the published image itself. From v26.4 on, t
 
 ---
 
-## Highlights for v26.8
+## Highlights for v26.9
 
-**The two families split on ROCm.** `rocm/primus` moves to the ROCm 10.1.0 release with PyTorch 2.14, and builds Transformer Engine and Flash Attention from source again. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20260923`) with JAX 0.11.1 and a Transformer Engine 2.18 development build, and **no longer ships a copy of Primus**: run it with a `release/v26.8` checkout, which `primus-cli container` mounts for you. Bare-metal installs changed accordingly — see [Bare-metal installation](./bare-metal-installation.md) and the [JAX guide](./bare-metal-installation-jax.md).
+**Both families move to ROCm nightlies.** `rocm/primus` moves from the ROCm 10.1.0 release to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20261020`), with a PyTorch 2.16 pre-release and a Transformer Engine 2.20 development build, still built from source. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.3 nightly (`10.3.0a20261026`) with JAX 0.12.0, a Transformer Engine 2.19 development build, and MaxText `release/v26.9`, and **ships a copy of Primus again**. Both images were built from the same Primus commit, `db1a4160` on `release/v26.9`—see [Primus source for v26.9](#primus-source-for-v269).
 
 ### Both families
 
+- **A convergence test for Megatron and MaxText.** `tools/convergence_test/` builds a dataset from a real corpus, lints the config for settings that silently spoil a convergence run (mock or synthetic data, forced load balancing, vocab mismatches), trains through the normal `primus-cli` path, plots the loss, and gates it against a previous release's baseline ([#1229](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1229)). It ships Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-2-7B, and Mixtral-8x7B recipes for both backends, plus a MaxText Llama-2-7B FP8 recipe for MI355X ([#1261](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1261)).
+- **The `tools/perf` batch runner is ready for unattended runs.** Each run is bounded by `MAX_RUN_SECONDS` (default 1 h) and `MAX_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 20 min); busy GPUs and bad network interfaces are refused up front; failures are classified with the log line that shows them; every result records the image, host, and platform it came from; diffusion and DLRM benchmarks join the batch; and results go into an Excel report that can compare against a baseline ([#1260](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1260), [#1266](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1266), [#1299](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1299)). Two misreported throughput values are fixed: TorchTitan values printed with a thousands separator, and Megatron-Bridge's post-training estimate. Note the behavior changes: single-node runs now time out, output files have fixed names, and the runners exit non-zero when any run fails.
+- **Release benchmark suites in the auto-benchmark menu.** One choice detects the GPU and runs the whole Primus suite (Megatron, Megatron Bridge, TorchTitan) or JAX suite (MaxText, MaxDiffusion), recording the image digest, Primus commit, and submodule pins with every result ([#1251](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1251)).
+- **A preset `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is kept.** The runner used to overwrite it with `0..GPUS_PER_NODE-1`, so on a shared node a job could land on another user's GPU; it now keeps your selection and warns when its count differs from `GPUS_PER_NODE` ([#1237](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1237)).
+
+### `rocm/primus`: Megatron-LM and TorchTitan
+
+#### Changes you might need to act on
+
+- **Mock-data runs use the model's real vocabulary.** Megatron mock data used to size every model for a 131,072-token vocabulary; each model config now sets its real `vocab_size`, so embeddings, output layer, and logits have their true size. Mock-data throughput and memory are therefore not comparable with earlier releases ([#1249](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1249)).
+- **Megatron-only example material moved under `examples/megatron/`.** For example `examples/deepseek-v4/` is now `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/`, and `examples/moe_package/` is now `examples/megatron/guides/moe_package/`; `examples/mlperf/` and `examples/hardware_configs/` stay where they were. Update scripts that name the old paths ([#1130](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1130)).
+- **Some environment switches are now config keys, and the old variables do nothing.** `PRIMUS_FUSED_QK_RMSNORM_ROPE` is replaced by `use_turbo_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope` ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)); `PRIMUS_TURBO_CROSS_ENTROPY` and `PRIMUS_TURBO_CE_OVERWRITE_INPUT` by `use_turbo_cross_entropy` and `turbo_ce_overwrite_input` ([#1245](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1245)); the MoE gather-quantization variables by `moe_permute_quant_fusion`, `moe_backward_permute_quant_fusion`, and `moe_skip_identity_sort` ([#1241](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1241)).
+- **Transformer Engine fused cross entropy reuses the logits buffer by default** (`te_ce_overwrite_input: true`), so after the loss backward the logits tensor holds its gradient. Set it to `false` when the same logits feed anything else in the step, such as a distillation or auxiliary loss, metrics, or hooks ([#1287](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1287)).
+- **TorchTitan uses a Triton fused AdamW by default** (`optimizer.use_triton_fused_adam: true`). Checkpoints stay interchangeable with `torch.optim.AdamW`; set the flag to `false` to go back to it. Reading `optimizer.state` directly between steps now shows stale `step` values ([#1233](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1233)).
+- **Turbo grouped GEMM expects expandable segments.** Primus warns when `use_turbo_grouped_gemm` is on without `expandable_segments:True`, and a runner hook stops the launch when `expandable_segments:True` is requested but not in effect on the PyTorch build ([#1257](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1257)).
+
+#### New features
+
+- **GLM-5.3-Flash** (`model_type: glm5_next`): KDA linear attention, DSA sparse attention, and manifold-constrained hyper-connections with a 288-expert MoE, an MI355X BF16 recipe, and online loading of the released Hugging Face checkpoint for any TP / EP / PP layout ([#1230](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1230)). Packed sequences now run under context parallelism ([#1265](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1265)) and text-only checkpoint exports load ([#1254](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1254)). Training was validated on an 8-layer proxy; the full 45-layer model was checked forward-only against SGLang, and its DSA indexer is frozen.
+- **ZAYA1-8B FP8 recipes** for MI300X, MI325X, and MI355X (`fp8: hybrid`, tensorwise scaling, accurate from a cold start) and an MI325X BF16 recipe ([#1269](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1269)); the MI355X micro-batch sizes now fill that GPU's memory ([#1279](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1279)).
+- **HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training**, stage 1 (geometry heads) and stage 2 (Gaussian head), with MI355X configs launched through `train posttrain`. The upstream trainer is the new `third_party/HunyuanWorld-Mirror-rocm` submodule; Primus applies ROCm fixes at runtime ([#1242](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1242)).
+- **MiniMax-M3 on MegaMoE.** The fused MegaMoE expert layer accepts MiniMax-M3's `swigluoai` activation and matches the DeepEP path's loss ([#1243](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1243)).
+- **Opt-in fusions:** Primus-Turbo fused cross entropy for TP1 training ([#1245](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1245)); FlyDSL Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE and residual RMSNorm + MXFP4 QKV fusions for GPT-OSS ([#1208](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1208)), with the fused Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE now also covering head dimension 128 ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)); and gradient reduce-scatter on the GPU's copy engines (`MEGATRON_GRAD_REDUCE_BACKEND=rccl_sdma`, which needs an RCCL build with CE ReduceScatter) ([#1207](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1207)).
+- **MI455X FP8 hybrid LoRA SFT proxies** for Llama-2-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, and Qwen3-235B-A22B on one GPU ([#1248](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1248)).

detail.body:
## Summary

Documentation for the v26.9 training images:

- `rocm/primus:v26.9` (Megatron-LM, TorchTitan, Megatron Bridge), built 2026-10-30
- `rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.9` (MaxText), built 2026-10-30

Both are built from Primus `db1a4160` on `release/v26.9`. The docs were written from the CI images that passed
QA, each probed under its release tag, with the release-docs-update skill.

**Stacked on #1374**, whose tools generated it: this PR targets `dev/release-docs-ci-images` and contains only
the 7 docs commits. It moves to `main` once #1374 is merged.

## Commits (one per phase)

1. **Image snapshots and release Dockerfiles**: `tools/release_docs/data/v26.9-{primus,jax}.json` and
   `.github/workflows/docker-release/Dockerfile.{primus,jax}-v26.9`, both taken from the images (the
   committed Dockerfiles match the images' baked-in copies).
2. **Version references** v26.8 → v26.9 across the docs, `README.md`, `runner/` and `primus/__init__.py`.
   References outside the documentation surface are kept: CI base images, example configs and their comments,
   tests, `tools/perf`.
3. **Release notes**: the v26.9 section (tables generated from the snapshots, the "Changes since v26.8" delta,
   Primus source) and the v26.9 Highlights for both families. The v26.8 Highlights move into the v26.8
   section; v26.6 leaves the detailed list.
4. **Recipe notes and new models**: "Important notes for v26.9" on the Megatron-LM, TorchTitan and MaxText
   pages, and the new recipes in the model lists and the model-support matrix (GLM-5.3-Flash,
   HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training, ZAYA1-8B FP8, MI325X ZAYA1-8B).
5. **Bare-metal install** re-pinned to the v26.9 Dockerfiles: `tools/installation*/setup.sh`, `env.sh`, the
   READMEs and the bare-metal guides.
6. **Review answers**: the JAX page no longer says the image ships no Primus (v26.9 bundles it again); history
   references restored to v26.8; the "Primus source" section notes that `release/v26.9` has moved past the
   build commit (`93dd9201`, MI325X GPT-OSS-20B and ZAYA1-8B tuning, #1355).
7. **Review edits**: the README "What's New" entry for v26.9, and a "Primus training performance" section in
   the overview linking AMD's published training results.

## Release highlights

**`rocm/primus:v26.9`**: a ROCm 10.2 nightly with a PyTorch 2.16 pre-release and a TransformerEngine 2.20
development build; new models (GLM-5.3-Flash, HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training, ZAYA1-8B FP8); a fused AdamW
optimizer by default in TorchTitan; MoE correctness fixes; mock-data benchmarks now use each model's real
vocabulary.

**`rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.9`**: JAX 0.12.0 and a TransformerEngine 2.19 development build on a ROCm 10.3
nightly; MaxText pinned to `release/v26.9`; Primus bundled in the image again; a lower default XLA autotuning
level fixes intermittent compile-time crashes.

Details and PR links are in `docs/01-getting-started/release-notes.md` under "Highlights for v26.9".

## Checks

- `release_notes.py check`: 123 values verified across all 6 documented images.
- `check_links.py` and `install_parity.py --check` pass.
- Bare-metal install and a 10-step training run of the v26.9 stacks passed on MI300X and MI355X for both
  families, from the same images, with the install scripts of #1374. They were not re-run on this exact branch.

## After merge

- Cherry-pick these commits to `release/v26.9`.
- Publish `rocm/primus:v26.9` and `rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.9`. The release notes already name these tags
  and their image IDs.

@@ -0,0 +1,629 @@
+ARG DEFAULT_BASE=ubuntu:24.04
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
+
+# uv: used as the installer for everything going into /opt/venv in jax_base
+# (faster resolves/installs than pip for this image's large ROCm/JAX/TE/torch
+# wheel sets). Pulled as a static binary from Astral's distroless image rather
+# than via pip. Needs its own named stage (rather than an ARG-interpolated
+# `COPY --from=` reference) since BuildKit doesn't support variable expansion
+# directly in --from.
+ARG UV_VERSION=0.12.7
+FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv_bin
+
+# rocm-sdk init (below) extracts a prebuilt bazelisk binary to /usr/local/bin/bazel
+# so ROCm/TheRock components can be rebuilt from source. That prebuilt binary is
+# stale (Go 1.23.0 stdlib, ~16 CVEs) and no newer official bazelisk release fixes
+# it either (still built with go1.24.0). Rebuild the same upstream source with a
+# current Go toolchain instead, preserving identical launcher behavior.
+FROM golang:1.26-bookworm AS bazelisk_builder
+ARG BAZELISK_VERSION=v1.29.0
+# bazelisk's own go.mod pins golang.org/x/crypto, golang.org/x/sys and
+# golang.org/x/net versions with known CVEs; bump them explicitly since no newer
+# bazelisk tag fixes this upstream. x/crypto uses a `replace` directive, not just
+# `go get`: as an indirect dep its require floor gets pulled back below the fix by
+# `go mod tidy`/MVS (observed drift to v0.54.0), while replace pins the build to
+# exactly v0.55.0. x/net is pinned exact (not -u) for the same drift reason.
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${BAZELISK_VERSION} https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazelisk.git /src \
+    && cd /src \
+    && go get -u golang.org/x/sys \
+    && go get golang.org/x/net@v0.56.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/crypto=golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 \
+    && go mod tidy \
+    && go build -o /bazelisk
+
+# transformer_engine_rocm_jax's own build vendors a copy of GoogleCloudPlatform/gcsfuse
+# (built to /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse) whose go.mod pins golang.org/x/text,
+# golang.org/x/net and google.golang.org/grpc versions with known CVEs; this isn't
+# fixed upstream as of gcsfuse's latest release, so rebuild the same binaries here
+# with those deps bumped and overwrite whatever TE's build (and later, MaxText's
+# apt-installed gcsfuse package) produced, preserving identical behavior. Both the
+# main gcsfuse binary and the mount.gcsfuse helper embed these deps, so both are
+# rebuilt. x/crypto and grpc use `replace` directives to force the CVE-fixed
+# versions past gcsfuse's own go.mod pins.
+FROM golang:1.26-bookworm AS gcsfuse_builder
+ARG GCSFUSE_VERSION=v3.11.2
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${GCSFUSE_VERSION} https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcsfuse.git /src \
+    && cd /src \
+    && go get golang.org/x/text@v0.39.0 \
+    && go get golang.org/x/net@v0.60.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace google.golang.org/grpc=google.golang.org/grpc@v1.83.2 \
+    && go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/crypto=golang.org/x/crypto@v0.57.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4=github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4@v4.1.6 \
+    && go mod tidy \
+    && go build -o /mount.gcsfuse ./tools/mount_gcsfuse \
+    && go build -o /gcsfuse .
+
+# pip's vendored msgpack, setuptools and urllib3 are flagged by Trivy via pip's SBOM
+# (pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json): GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964, CVE-2025-47273, CVE-2026-97687/97689.
+# Rebuild pip with msgpack 1.2.3, urllib3 2.8.0 and setuptools 79.0.1 (highest that
+# satisfies pip's `setuptools<80` vendor pin) so the regenerated SBOM is clean.
+FROM python:3.12-slim AS pip_builder
+ARG PIP_VERSION=26.2.2
+# build-essential: msgpack has no pure "any" wheel, so `vendoring sync` builds it
+# from sdist and needs a C compiler; the compiled .so is dropped afterward per
+# pip's own vendoring config, leaving the pure-Python copy pip ships.
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git build-essential \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && pip install vendoring build
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${PIP_VERSION} https://github.com/pypa/pip.git /src
+WORKDIR /src
+RUN sed -i \
+        -e 's/^msgpack==.*/msgpack==1.2.3/' \
+        -e 's/^setuptools==.*/setuptools==79.0.1/' \
+        -e 's/^\( *\)urllib3==.*/\1urllib3==2.8.0/' \
+        src/pip/_vendor/vendor.txt
+# setuptools 79.0.1's pkg_resources uses dotted `import packaging.<sub>` imports
+# that vendoring can't rewrite into the pip._vendor namespace, plus a bare
+# `from jaraco.text import ...` (jaraco isn't vendored). Overwrite pip's own
+# vendoring patch (pinned to 70.3.0) with one that runs during `vendoring sync`,
+# before its import-transform step: rewrite the dotted packaging imports to
+# pip._vendor.packaging.<sub> and redirect jaraco to pip's bundled _jaraco_text
+# shim. platformdirs is a plain `from platformdirs import ...` and is rewritten
+# automatically. Built via printf so the diff's leading context space survives.
+RUN printf '%s\n' \
+        '--- a/src/pip/_vendor/pkg_resources/__init__.py' \
+        '+++ b/src/pip/_vendor/pkg_resources/__init__.py' \
+        '@@ -85,7 +85,8 @@' \
+        '-import packaging.markers' \
+        '-import packaging.requirements' \
+        '-import packaging.specifiers' \
+        '-import packaging.utils' \
+        '-import packaging.version' \
+        '-from jaraco.text import drop_comment, join_continuation, yield_lines' \
+        '+from pip._vendor import packaging' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.markers' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.requirements' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.specifiers' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.utils' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.version' \
+        '+from pip._internal.utils._jaraco_text import drop_comment, join_continuation, yield_lines' \
+        ' from platformdirs import user_cache_dir as _user_cache_dir' \
+        > tools/vendoring/patches/pkg_resources.patch \
+    && vendoring sync -v \
+    && python -m build --wheel -o /dist
+
+FROM  ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS jax_base
+
+WORKDIR /workspace/
+ENV MAX_JOBS=128
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+ENV ROCM_AMDGPU_TARGETS="gfx942,gfx950"
+
+# Flag to fix profiler hang issue.
+ENV ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0
+ENV DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=0
+
+# Install Ubuntu dependencies
+ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+# linux-libc-dev, openssl and libssl3t64 come pre-installed in the base image; upgrade
+# just them (not a blanket `apt upgrade`) for kernel-header/openssl CVEs (CVE-2026-84782).
+# Bump LIBC_SECURITY_REFRESH to bust this layer's cache, else it stays frozen at the
+# versions current when it was last built.
+ARG LIBC_SECURITY_REFRESH=2026-10-01
+RUN echo "base security refresh: ${LIBC_SECURITY_REFRESH}" \
+	&& apt update \
+	&& apt install --only-upgrade --no-install-recommends -y linux-libc-dev openssl libssl3t64 \
+	&& apt install -y --no-install-recommends \
+	gfortran \
+	git \
+	git-lfs \
+	ninja-build \
+	g++ \
+	pkg-config \
+	xxd \
+	patchelf \
+	automake \
+	libtool \
+	python3-venv \
+	python3-dev \
+	python-is-python3 \
+	libegl1-mesa-dev \
+	wget \
+    sudo \
+    flex \
+    liblzma-dev \
+    ccache \
+    libdw1 \
+    libdrm-dev \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+COPY --from=uv_bin /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
+
+# Setup python env
+RUN uv venv /opt/venv --python 3.12
+ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
+ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
+# wheel and setuptools are pinned for CVE fixes (setuptools>=80.10.2 also vendors
+# patched copies of wheel/jaraco.context internally); msgpack likewise. These are
+# re-forced again after the Primus install further down, since Primus/maxtext
+# transitively pull in older, CVE-affected copies of all three.
+# urllib3==2.8.0 (CVE-2026-97687/97689) is pinned before the ROCm SDK install because
+# the rocm-sdk wheels pull in 2.7.0, which Trivy flags in that layer even if a later
+# layer upgrades it.
+# Install pip from the re-vendored wheel built in pip_builder (patched msgpack +
+# setuptools in pip/_vendor). pip itself is kept in the venv (even though uv
+# drives every install here) because MaxText's setup.sh bootstraps and invokes
+# `pip` directly. --reinstall since the wheel shares the 26.2.1 version string,
+# so a plain install would no-op.
+COPY --from=pip_builder /dist/pip-*.whl /tmp/
+RUN uv pip install --reinstall /tmp/pip-*.whl \
+    && rm -f /tmp/pip-*.whl \
+    && uv pip uninstall wheel \
+    && uv pip install \
+        cmake==3.31.6 \
+        ninja==1.11.1.3 \
+        wheel==0.46.2 \
+        packaging==25.0 \
+        setuptools==80.10.2 \
+        msgpack==1.2.3 \
+        urllib3==2.8.0 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Install ROCm and related libraries from the rock pip wheels
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next/rocm/
+ENV THE_ROCK_VERSION=10.3.0a20261026
+
+# Note: we need to ensure all the ROCm packages are installed with the same version to avoid
+# potential issues. However, right now during the nightly sweep we only look at the latest version
+# rocm. If we ever run into issues, we can consider sweeping all the ROCm packages and pinning them
+# to a common latest version.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --pre \
+        rocm==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-bootstrap \
+        rocm-sdk-core==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-devel==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx942==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx950==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-libraries==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+RUN rocm-sdk init \
+    # Workaround: rocm-sdk-core and rocm-sdk-devel both ship libamd_comgr.so.3
+    # as separate inodes, causing duplicate LLVM static constructor registration
+    # (spirv-expand-step registered twice -> SIGABRT). The ln -f must be in the
+    # same RUN as the pip install so both files are in the same writable overlayfs
+    # layer. A separate RUN would copy-up instead of hardlink, leaving two inodes.
+    # Fix belongs in TheRock: rocm-sdk-devel should not ship its own comgr copy.
+    # See: https://amd-hub.atlassian.net/browse/AIMA-248
+    && ln -sf \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3 \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3
+COPY --from=bazelisk_builder /bazelisk /usr/local/bin/bazel
+ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+# Note: Primus uses `ROCM_HOME` instead of `ROCM_PATH`. Set both to avoid potential issues.
+ENV ROCM_HOME=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+ENV HIP_PLATFORM=amd
+ENV HIP_PATH=$ROCM_PATH
+ENV HIP_CLANG_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/llvm/bin
+ENV HIP_INCLUDE_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/include
+ENV HIP_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib
+ENV HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode
+ENV PATH="$ROCM_PATH/bin:$HIP_CLANG_PATH:$PATH"
+ENV LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64"
+ENV CPATH=$HIP_INCLUDE_PATH
+ENV PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$ROCM_PATH/lib/pkgconfig"
+
+# TE 2.17 + jax segfault fix: blank LD_LIBRARY_PATH for the shipped runtime.
+# The rocm-sdk-devel lib dirs put on LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the jax_base stage are
+# needed at build time (hipcc / RCCL / UCX / OpenMPI must find ROCm), but at
+# runtime they shadow the ROCm libs that transformer_engine_rocm_jax and
+# jax_rocm7_plugin bundle and reference via their wheel RPATH. That loads two
+# mismatched copies of the HIP/ROCm runtime, and the CK-JIT fmha_bwd kernel
+# dlopen segfaults inside the first pjit step on gfx950. Clearing it here --
+# after every build step -- lets each wheel resolve ROCm through its own RPATH.
+# The in-place RCCL override in jax_base does not depend on LD_LIBRARY_PATH, so
+# it is unaffected.
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=""
+
+# JAX
+# Note: JAX and related libraries need to be installed before TE
+ARG JAX_VERSION=0.12.0
+ENV JAX_VERSION=${JAX_VERSION}
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/jax/whl-next/jax-rocm10-pjrt/
+ENV JAX_PJRT_VERSION=0.12.0+rocm10.3.0a20261026
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/jax/whl-next/jax-rocm10-plugin/
+ENV JAX_PLUGIN_VERSION=0.12.0+rocm10.3.0a20261026
+
+RUN uv pip install jax==${JAX_VERSION} jaxlib==${JAX_VERSION} scipy==1.16 \
+    && uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/jax/whl-next/ \
+        --pre \
+        jax_rocm10_pjrt==${JAX_PJRT_VERSION} \
+        jax_rocm10_plugin==${JAX_PLUGIN_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# TransformerEngine
+# See: https://rocm.frameworks-nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch-staging/transformer-engine-rocm-jax/
+ARG TE_VERSION=2.19.0.dev0+rocm10.2.0a20261002.bfe94fb
+
+# flaxlib_src (bundled inside the flax wheel) is inert vendored Rust/C++ reference
+# source: flax only imports the compiled flaxlib extension when flax_use_flaxlib is
+# enabled (default off), and no such extension is ever built here, so it's unreachable
+# either way. Delete it below to drop its Cargo.lock (stale pyo3 CVE) with no behavior
+# change. This pin/deletion is repeated again after the Primus install further down,
+# since Primus transitively pulls in a newer flax that reintroduces flaxlib_src.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        pybind11==3.0.4 \
+        importlib-metadata==8.7.1 \
+        pydantic==2.13.4 \
+        flax==0.12.10 \
+    && uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://rocm.frameworks-nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch-staging/ \
+        --pre \
+        --no-build-isolation \
+        transformer_engine_rocm_jax==${TE_VERSION} \
+        transformer-engine-rocm10==${TE_VERSION} \
+    && sed -i 's|transformer-engine-rocm7|transformer-engine-rocm7", "transformer-engine-rocm10|g' \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformer_engine/common/__init__.py \
+    && find /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/orbax -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && rm -rf /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flaxlib_src \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+COPY --from=gcsfuse_builder /mount.gcsfuse /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse
+
+FROM jax_base AS jax_training
+
+# Intentionally root (no USER instruction): training entrypoints need direct
+# access to /dev/kfd and /dev/dri GPU device nodes and to AINIC/RDMA devices,
+# which a non-root user cannot reliably get across the container runtimes this
+# image is deployed on. Trivy DS-0002 is expected to keep flagging this;
+# tracked as an accepted risk rather than remediated here.
+
+# Configure required envs
+ENV NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=1
+ENV NVTE_USE_HIPBLASLT=1
+ENV GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+ENV HSA_FORCE_FINE_GRAIN_PCIE=1
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
+ENV NCCL_DEBUG=VERSION
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_BWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_FWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_IS_V3_ATOMIC_FP32=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_HOW_V3_BF16_CVT=2
+ENV XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=.9
+ENV XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor=95 --xla_gpu_reduce_scatter_combine_threshold_bytes=8589934592 --xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler=True --xla_gpu_all_gather_combine_threshold_bytes=8589934592 --xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=False --xla_gpu_enable_cublaslt=True --xla_gpu_autotune_level=0 --xla_gpu_enable_all_gather_combine_by_dim=FALSE --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=''"
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Install maxtext
+ARG MAXTEXT_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/maxtext.git
+ARG MAXTEXT_BRANCH=release/v26.9
+
+RUN git clone ${MAXTEXT_REPO} \
+    && cd maxtext \
+    && git checkout ${MAXTEXT_BRANCH} \
+    && chmod +x src/dependencies/scripts/setup.sh \
+    && ./src/dependencies/scripts/setup.sh TF=true \
+    && cd .. \
+    && find maxtext -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Make the clone above the one MaxText-consuming tools resolve to. Primus picks its
+# MaxText backend from MAXTEXT_PATH and otherwise falls back to its own
+# third_party/maxtext submodule, which pins whatever release Primus/main tracks
+# rather than MAXTEXT_BRANCH -- so without this a run silently tests the wrong
+# MaxText. Set as ENV (not just in the CI scripts) so every entrypoint in the image
+# inherits it. Primus's own bare-metal installer exports the same var for this reason
+# (Primus tools/installation-jax/env.sh).
+ENV MAXTEXT_PATH=/workspace/maxtext
+
+# Fix (root cause): the prebuilt PyPI TensorFlow wheel bundles an LLVM whose symbols
+# collide with ROCm 7.14's libLLVM inside Grain "spawn" workers -> SIGSEGV on
+# `import tensorflow` after `import jax`. Rebuild the CPU-only TF wheel from ROCm's
+# fork (correct symbol visibility) and install it in place of the stock wheel. A CPU
+# build also has no bundled NCCL, so it preserves the previous XLA-RCCL fix.
+# NOTE: bumps TF to 2.21.0 and adds a long (~30-60 min) bazel build to the image.
+# bazel is already installed via the bazelisk_builder stage above (jax_base ->
+# jax_training inherits /usr/local/bin/bazel) -- reused here rather than
+# re-downloading the vulnerable prebuilt bazelisk release.
+ARG TF_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/tensorflow-upstream.git
+ARG TF_BRANCH=upstream-v2.21.0
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip zip \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+# GitHub's on-the-fly gzip for the pinned LLVM archive has an unstable checksum that breaks
+# the TF build. Pull a frozen copy from our ACR and feed Bazel via --distdir (no network fetch).
+COPY --from=unifiedtrainingdockers.azurecr.io/utd/mirror:llvm-909041e4802c4b9a2223ca04099f35bf1dbbd460 \
+    /909041e4802c4b9a2223ca04099f35bf1dbbd460.tar.gz /opt/bazel_distdir/
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${TF_BRANCH} ${TF_REPO} tensorflow-upstream \
+    && cd tensorflow-upstream \
+    && grep -q 3f986184ee126677dbd77edb16d6b82c057ec869fefd7a9871979941e52e837a \
+        third_party/xla/third_party/llvm/workspace.bzl \

+# Primus
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus.git
+# Latest commit on `release/v26.9` branch. Commited on 2026-10-30.
+ARG PRIMUS_BRANCH=db1a41601833294231daadb3cdbb2933eb805c73
+
+RUN git clone --recurse-submodules ${PRIMUS_REPO} \
+    && cd Primus \
+    && git checkout ${PRIMUS_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init third_party/maxtext/ \
+    && cd .. \
+    && find Primus -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && uv pip uninstall dataclasses dataclasses_json \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# maxtext/Primus pull these in transitively at older, CVE-affected versions.
+# Force the fixed versions found by Trivy. setuptools>=80.10.2 also vendors
+# patched copies of wheel (0.46.3) and jaraco.context (6.1.0) internally,
+# resolving the two vendored-copy CVEs that the top-level wheel pin above
+# can't reach. flax is re-pinned and flaxlib_src re-deleted here too: Primus's
+# install above transitively upgrades flax past the pin/deletion done earlier
+# in the jax_base stage, undoing that fix. cryptography is bumped past 48.0.1
+# for CVE-2026-69247/CVE-2026-69249 (Trivy), both disclosed after that pin was
+# first set. keras is pulled in transitively by tensorflow (via maxtext's
+# setup.sh); 3.14.1 is CVE-2026-12481/CVE-2026-12484 (arbitrary code
+# execution via unsafe deserialization), fixed in 3.15.0. jax/jaxlib are
+# re-pinned to JAX_VERSION here as a guardrail: uv's --upgrade re-resolves
+# ALL packages (unlike pip's --upgrade, which only touches named ones), and
+# without an explicit pin it silently bumps jax 0.11.0 -> 0.11.1. 0.11.1
+# drops jax.experimental.hijax.MutableHiType, which flax 0.12.8 imports at
+# load time, breaking every maxtext GPU test. nltk is pulled transitively by
+# maxtext at 3.10.0; 3.10.3 fixes CVE-2026-79675 (CRITICAL) and CVE-2026-78680
+# (Trivy), both disclosed after these pins were set. urllib3 is re-forced in case
+# setup.sh re-resolves it; virtualenv 21.14.13 (CVE-2026-102930/102925) comes in via MaxText.
+RUN uv pip install --upgrade \
+        pillow==13.0.0 \
+        starlette==1.3.1 \
+        pyasn1==0.6.4 \
+        cryptography==50.0.0 \
+        httplib2==0.32.0 \
+        aiohttp==3.14.4 \
+        urllib3==2.8.0 \
+        virtualenv==21.14.13 \
+        filelock==4.2.4 \
+        black==26.10.1 \
+        msgpack==1.2.3 \
+        setuptools==80.10.2 \
+        flax==0.12.10 \
+        keras==3.15.0 \
+        nltk==3.10.4 \
+        oauthlib==4.0.0 \
+        jax==${JAX_VERSION} \
+        jaxlib==${JAX_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flaxlib_src \
+    && find /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pathwaysutils -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \

+# MaxText's setup.sh (cloned above) installs Google's official gcsfuse apt
+# package, which overwrites our deps-bumped mount.gcsfuse (COPY'd earlier in

+# could touch them — so these are the final bytes on disk.
+COPY --from=gcsfuse_builder /mount.gcsfuse /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse

+    && apt install -y --no-install-recommends \
+    libibverbs-dev \
+    jq \
+    dpkg-dev \
+    kmod \
+    xz-utils \
+    ibverbs-utils \
+    infiniband-diags \
+    rdma-core \
+    ethtool \
+    libevent-dev \
+    libhwloc-dev \
+    libmunge-dev \

+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

+# Install AMD AINIC library. The libionic user-space provider must match the host's
+# AINIC (ionic) driver: 1.117.5-a-56 and later speak ionic ABI 1, older bundles ABI 4.

+RUN wget https://github.com/openucx/ucx/releases/download/v${UCX_VERSION}/ucx-${UCX_VERSION}.tar.gz \
+    && mkdir -p ucx-${UCX_VERSION} \
+    && tar -zxf ucx-${UCX_VERSION}.tar.gz -C ucx-${UCX_VERSION} --strip-components=1 \

+    && cd build \

+RUN wget https://download.open-mpi.org/release/open-mpi/v$(echo "${MPI_VERSION}" | cut -d. -f1-2)/openmpi-${MPI_VERSION}.tar.gz \
+    && mkdir -p ompi-${MPI_VERSION} \
+    && tar -zxf openmpi-${MPI_VERSION}.tar.gz -C ompi-${MPI_VERSION} --strip-components=1 \

+    && cd build \

+    && cd ../.. \

+####### End of AINIC related installations #######
+
+# Secret scan will complain those files to be secrets. Explicitly remove them.
+RUN rm -f /workspace/Primus/.git/packed-refs /workspace/Primus/.git/modules/third_party/**/packed-refs
+
+# Clean cache
+RUN rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Training docker manifest
+ARG GIT_COMMIT_TAG=DEV
+ARG DOCKERFILE_PATH=Dockerfile
+
+# Copy patch files for training docker versioning
+RUN mkdir -p /workspace/.manifest \

+    && uv pip list > /workspace/.manifest/requirements.txt \

+COPY ${DOCKERFILE_PATH} /workspace/.manifest/docker-build-recipe.txt

+FROM jax_training AS jax_maxdiffusion

+# ========================================================================
+# MaxDiffusion additions (WAN 2.1 + FLUX.1-dev) on top of jax_training.
+# jax_training already ships JAX, Transformer Engine, MaxText and its JAX
+# ecosystem libs (flax, drjax, qwix, tokamax, einshape, typeguard,
+# transformers, tensorflow), so only the still-missing/incompatible pieces
+# are handled below. torch, torchvision, scikit-image and imageio-ffmpeg are
+# absent from jax_training; transformers ships as v5 there and is pinned
+# back to 4.57.3 below.
+# ========================================================================
+
+# jax_training's WORKDIR (/workspace) carries over from jax_base, so no need
+# to mkdir/WORKDIR again here.
+
+# Force Transformer Engine to load ONLY its JAX extension. jax_training's TE
+# build defaults to _use_pytorch=True and, once we install torch below,
+# eagerly imports transformer_engine.pytorch. Because jax_training ships only
+# the JAX/core TE wheels (transformer_engine_rocm_jax / transformer_engine_rocm7)
+# and NOT transformer_engine_rocm_torch, that import raises "AssertionError:
+# Found `transformer-engine` PyPI package but not transformer_engine_rocm_torch"
+# the moment maxdiffusion enters transformer_engine_context(). NVTE_FRAMEWORK=jax
+# skips the torch extension.
+ENV NVTE_FRAMEWORK=jax
+
+# MaxDiffusion dependencies: torch/torchvision for video processing.
+# torch deps are already present in jax_training, so --no-index is safe;
+# TheRock wheels: includes _rocm_init which resolves ROCm libs via rocm_sdk
+# at import time, eliminating the need for LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
+RUN uv pip install --no-deps \
+    --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+    "torch==2.15.0+rocm10.3.0a20261026" \
+    "torchvision==0.29.2+rocm10.3.0a20261026" \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+RUN uv pip install \
+    scikit-image \
+    imageio-ffmpeg \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# MaxDiffusion imports the Flax CLIP classes (FlaxCLIPTextModel) which were
+# removed in transformers v5. jax_training ships transformers 5.x, so pin
+# back to the last Flax-capable 4.x release (matches the previously-working
+# setup).
+# 4.57.3 carries two HIGH CVEs (CVE-2026-4372, CVE-2026-5241) only fixed at
+# transformers>=5.3.0/5.5.0 -- no 4.x backport exists, and bumping to 5.x isn't an
+# option here (see above). Accepted as risk: CVE-2026-4372's RCE path requires the
+# optional `kernels` package, which is never installed in this image (MaxDiffusion
+# itself is installed --no-deps below); CVE-2026-5241's RCE path is specific to
+# loading LightGlue via trust_remote_code, which MaxDiffusion's diffusion/video
+# pipelines never do. Neither exploit precondition is present here.
+RUN uv pip install transformers==4.57.3 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# The FLUX text encoder uses transformers' Flax T5, which calls
+# jnp.clip(..., a_max=...). JAX 0.10 removed the a_min/a_max kwargs (renamed to
+# min/max), so this raises "clip() got an unexpected keyword argument 'a_max'".
+# Patch the two jnp.clip calls in the Flax T5 model to the new kwarg names.
+RUN sed -i 's/a_max=/max=/g; s/a_min=/min=/g' \
+    /opt/venv/lib/python*/site-packages/transformers/models/t5/modeling_flax_t5.py
+
+# Clone and install MaxDiffusion
+ARG MAXDIFFUSION_REPO=https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/maxdiffusion.git
+ARG MAXDIFFUSION_COMMIT=68e069659f0af80694559e29939a17f879fe7f6a
+RUN git clone ${MAXDIFFUSION_REPO} /workspace/maxdiffusion && \
+    cd /workspace/maxdiffusion && \
+    git checkout ${MAXDIFFUSION_COMMIT} && \
+    uv pip install -e . --no-deps && \
+    find /workspace/maxdiffusion -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete && \
+    rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Transformer Engine and TensorFlow have a library-load order conflict on
+# jax_training: importing TE before TF segfaults at TF's C-extension preload.
+# Every maxdiffusion entrypoint imports jax, then enters
+# transformer_engine_context() (which imports TE) before the trainer pulls in
+# TF. Preload TF inside that context so the load order is always
+# jax -> tensorflow -> transformer_engine.
+RUN sed -i \
+    '/from transformer_engine.jax.sharding import global_shard_guard, MeshResource/i\    import tensorflow  # noqa: F401 preload before Transformer Engine to avoid segfault' \
+    /workspace/maxdiffusion/src/maxdiffusion/train_utils.py
+
+# cudnn_flash_te attention: maxdiffusion disables the Shardy partitioner to fall
+# back to GSPMD, but jax_training ships JAX 0.10+ + Transformer Engine, where
+# TE registers its custom_partitioner with a Shardy sharding_rule ONLY (GSPMD's
+# infer_sharding_from_operands is dropped for JAX > 0.9.1). Forcing GSPMD makes
+# XLA call a None infer_sharding_from_operands -> "'NoneType' object is not
+# callable" abort during sharding propagation. Keep Shardy enabled (the JAX
+# 0.10+ default, and what maxdiffusion's generate_wan.py already uses) so TE's
+# Shardy rule is honored.
+RUN sed -i \
+    's/jax.config.update("jax_use_shardy_partitioner", False)/jax.config.update("jax_use_shardy_partitioner", True)/g' \
+    /workspace/maxdiffusion/src/maxdiffusion/models/attention_flax.py
+
+# cudnn_flash_te attention: TE's fused-attention partitioner aborts with
+# "AssertionError:  is not a axis of the given mesh" during XLA compilation on
+# jax_training's TE build. TE resolves the context-parallel axis via
+# _maybe_context_parallel_axis(), which only reads MeshResource.cp_resource
+# when is_mesh_available() is True; at attention config-build time that is
+# False, so cp_axis is frozen as "" (empty) even though maxdiffusion sets
+# cp_resource="context". At partition time get_mesh_axis_size("") then fails
+# its `axis in mesh.shape` assertion. TE already treats `axis is None` as size
+# 1 (i.e. no context parallelism); extend that to the empty string so an
+# unresolved cp_axis means "no CP" (correct here, context mesh dim = 1)
+# instead of crashing.
+RUN sed -i \
+    's|    assert axis in mesh.shape, f"{axis} is not a axis of the given mesh {mesh.shape}"|    if not axis:\n        return 1\n    assert axis in mesh.shape, f"{axis} is not a axis of the given mesh {mesh.shape}"|' \
+    /opt/venv/lib/python*/site-packages/transformer_engine/jax/sharding.py
+
+RUN uv pip list
