+# Primus Training Dockerfile for ROCm on TheRock
+ARG DEFAULT_BASE=ubuntu:24.04
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
+
+# uv: used as the installer for everything going into /opt/venv (faster
+# resolves/installs than pip for this image's large ROCm/PyTorch/TE wheel sets).
+# Pulled as a static binary from Astral's distroless image rather than via pip.
+# Needs its own named stage (rather than an ARG-interpolated `COPY --from=`
+# reference) since BuildKit doesn't support variable expansion directly in --from.
+ARG UV_VERSION=0.12.7
+FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv_bin
+
+# The wandb-core Go binary shipped inside the wandb wheel is flagged by Trivy for
+# CVEs in the Go stdlib and in a vendored third-party module, google.golang.org/grpc.
+# Since the build uses -mod=vendor, grpc has to be bumped explicitly in go.mod and
+# vendor/ regenerated to clear it properly.
+FROM golang:1.27-bookworm AS wandb_core_builder
+ARG WANDB_VERSION=v0.28.2
+ARG GRPC_VERSION=v1.83.2
+ARG XNET_VERSION=v0.60.0
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${WANDB_VERSION} https://github.com/wandb/wandb.git /src \
+    && cd /src/core \
+    && GOTOOLCHAIN=local go get google.golang.org/grpc@${GRPC_VERSION} \
+    && GOTOOLCHAIN=local go get golang.org/x/net@${XNET_VERSION} \
+    && GOTOOLCHAIN=local go mod vendor \
+    && CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build \
+        -tags "disable_grpc_modules parquet_read_only" \
+        -ldflags="-s -w -X main.commit=${WANDB_VERSION}" \
+        -mod=vendor \
+        -o /wandb-core \
+        cmd/wandb-core/main.go
+
+# pip vendors its own copies of msgpack, setuptools and urllib3 under pip/_vendor,
+# declared in the SBOM it ships, which Trivy flags for known vulnerabilities.
+# Rebuild pip with them bumped past the fixes -- msgpack 1.2.3 (CVE-2026-114613),
+# urllib3 2.8.0 (CVE-2026-97687/CVE-2026-97689), setuptools 79.0.1 (the highest allowed by
+# pip's own `setuptools<80` vendor pin). urllib3 is indented under requests in
+# vendor.txt, so its sed keeps the leading whitespace. pip 26.2.2 already vendors
+# certifi 2026.10.19 (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2), so certifi needs no sed.
+FROM python:3.12-slim AS pip_builder
+ARG PIP_VERSION=26.2.2
+# build-essential: msgpack has no pure "any" wheel, so `vendoring sync` builds it
+# from sdist and needs a C compiler; the compiled .so is dropped afterward per
+# pip's own vendoring config, leaving the pure-Python copy pip ships.
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git build-essential \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && pip install vendoring build
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${PIP_VERSION} https://github.com/pypa/pip.git /src
+WORKDIR /src
+RUN sed -i \
+        -e 's/^msgpack==.*/msgpack==1.2.3/' \
+        -e 's/^setuptools==.*/setuptools==79.0.1/' \
+        -e 's/^\( *\)urllib3==.*/\1urllib3==2.8.0/' \
+        src/pip/_vendor/vendor.txt
+# setuptools 79.0.1's pkg_resources uses dotted `import packaging.<sub>` imports
+# that vendoring can't rewrite into the pip._vendor namespace, plus a bare
+# `from jaraco.text import ...` (jaraco isn't vendored). Overwrite pip's own
+# vendoring patch (pinned to 70.3.0) with one that runs during `vendoring sync`,
+# before its import-transform step: rewrite the dotted packaging imports to
+# pip._vendor.packaging.<sub> and redirect jaraco to pip's bundled _jaraco_text
+# shim. platformdirs is a plain `from platformdirs import ...` and is rewritten
+# automatically. Built via printf so the diff's leading context space survives.
+RUN printf '%s\n' \
+        '--- a/src/pip/_vendor/pkg_resources/__init__.py' \
+        '+++ b/src/pip/_vendor/pkg_resources/__init__.py' \
+        '@@ -85,7 +85,8 @@' \
+        '-import packaging.markers' \
+        '-import packaging.requirements' \
+        '-import packaging.specifiers' \
+        '-import packaging.utils' \
+        '-import packaging.version' \
+        '-from jaraco.text import drop_comment, join_continuation, yield_lines' \
+        '+from pip._vendor import packaging' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.markers' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.requirements' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.specifiers' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.utils' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.version' \
+        '+from pip._internal.utils._jaraco_text import drop_comment, join_continuation, yield_lines' \
+        ' from platformdirs import user_cache_dir as _user_cache_dir' \
+        > tools/vendoring/patches/pkg_resources.patch \
+    && vendoring sync -v \
+    && python -m build --wheel -o /dist
+
+FROM  ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
+
+WORKDIR /workspace/
+ENV MAX_JOBS=128
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+ENV ROCM_AMDGPU_TARGETS="gfx942,gfx950"
+ENV GPU_ARCHS="${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}"
+ENV MLPERF_RUNTIME_SERIES=v26.5
+
+# Install Ubuntu dependencies
+ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --only-upgrade --no-install-recommends -y linux-libc-dev \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y \
+    gfortran \
+    git \
+    git-lfs \
+    ninja-build \
+    g++ \
+    pkg-config \
+    xxd \
+    patchelf \
+    automake \
+    libtool \
+    python3-venv \
+    python3-dev \
+    python-is-python3 \
+    libegl1-mesa-dev \
+    wget \
+    sudo \
+    flex \
+    liblzma-dev \
+    ccache \
+    libdw1 \
+    libdrm-dev \
+    iproute2 \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Setup python env
+COPY --from=uv_bin /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
+RUN uv venv /opt/venv --python 3.12
+ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
+ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
+# wheel and setuptools are pinned for CVE fixes (setuptools>=80.10.2 also carries
+# fixed vendored copies of wheel/jaraco.context); other versions are unrelated pins.
+# Install pip from the re-vendored wheel built in pip_builder (patched msgpack +
+# setuptools in pip/_vendor), which clears the Trivy GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 (msgpack)
+# and CVE-2025-47273 (setuptools) findings against pip's vendored SBOM at the
+# source. pip is kept in the venv (even though uv drives every install here)
+# because the two source builds below (mamba, FBGEMM) run `python setup.py
+# install`, which needs setuptools/pip present. --reinstall since the
+# wheel shares the 26.2.1 version string, so a plain install would no-op.
+COPY --from=pip_builder /dist/pip-*.whl /tmp/
+RUN uv pip install --reinstall /tmp/pip-*.whl \
+    && rm -f /tmp/pip-*.whl \
+    && uv pip install \
+        pybind11 \
+        typeguard \
+        wheel==0.46.2 \
+        cmake==3.31.6 \
+        ninja==1.11.1.3 \
+        packaging==25.0 \
+        setuptools==80.10.2 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y \
+        ninja-build \
+        autoconf \
+        libtool \
+        flex \
+        rdma-core \
+        ffmpeg \
+        patch \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Workaround for the HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES issue
+ENV HSA_ENABLE_SCRATCH_ASYNC_RECLAIM=0
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+
+# Enable the device (AQL) queue path
+ENV GPU_USE_DEVICE_QUEUE=1
+ENV DEBUG_CLR_AQL_DEV_QUEUE=1
+
+# Requested alongside Primus #1286 to resolve memory issues.
+ENV TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0
+
+# Install ROCm and related libraries from the rock pip wheels
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next/rocm/
+ENV THE_ROCK_VERSION=10.2.0a20261020
+
+# Note: we need to ensure all the ROCm packages are installed with the same version to avoid
+# potential issues. However, right now during the nightly sweep we only look at the latest version
+# rocm. If we ever run into issues, we can consider sweeping all the ROCm packages and pinning them
+# to a common latest version.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --pre \
+        rocm==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-bootstrap \
+        rocm-sdk-core==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-devel==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx942==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx950==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-libraries==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Pytorch
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/torch/
+ARG PYTORCH_VERSION=2.16.0a0+rocm10.2.0a20261020
+
+# fsspec 2026.6.0 fixes CVE-2026-104851 (Trivy); it needs datasets>=5.0.1 below,
+# since datasets 3.x caps fsspec<=2025.3.0. s3fs follows fsspec's version.
+# datasets stays at 5.0.1: 5.1.0 needs pyarrow>=24, but Primus pins pyarrow==21.0.0.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        cxxfilt==0.3.0 \
+        tqdm==4.67.3 \
+        pyyaml==6.0.3 \
+        pytest==9.0.3 \
+        matplotlib==3.10.9 \
+        pandas==2.3.3 \
+        py-cpuinfo==9.0.0 \
+        build==1.5.0 \
+        filelock==4.2.1 \
+        sympy==1.14.0 \
+        networkx==3.6.1 \
+        jinja2==3.1.6 \
+        fsspec==2026.6.0 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# torchaudio has no amd-torchaudio-device anchor, so it won't auto-match torch's rock build; pin it explicitly.
+RUN uv pip uninstall torch && \
+    uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+        --pre \
+        torch==${PYTORCH_VERSION} \
+        amd-torch-device-gfx942==${PYTORCH_VERSION} \
+        amd-torch-device-gfx950==${PYTORCH_VERSION} \
+        torchaudio==2.11.0a0+rocm${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        torchvision==0.30.0a0+rocm${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        amd-torchvision-device-gfx942==0.30.0a0+rocm${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        amd-torchvision-device-gfx950==0.30.0a0+rocm${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        apex \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# apex ships a lazy JIT shim (fused_weight_gradient_mlp_cuda.py) that compiles the
+# fused wgrad kernel at runtime via apex/op_builder/builder.py, which hardcodes
+# -std=c++17 in both its cxx and ROCm nvcc args. torch 2.15 requires C++20, so the
+# runtime JIT build fails (#error C++20 or later ...). Force c++20 in apex's builder.
+RUN sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/g' \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/apex/op_builder/builder.py
+
+# torch 2.16 (pytorch/pytorch#194641) added a ROCm hipify warning in CUDAExtension that
+# calls source.endswith(), which crashes on pathlib.Path sources (Primus-Turbo passes Path:
+# AttributeError: 'PosixPath' object has no attribute 'endswith'). Coerce to str. No-op on
+# torch 2.15 and once upstream fixes it.
+RUN sed -i 's/if source\.endswith((/if str(source).endswith((/' \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/utils/cpp_extension.py
+
+RUN rocm-sdk init \
+    # Workaround: rocm-sdk-core and rocm-sdk-devel both ship libamd_comgr.so.3
+    # as separate inodes, causing duplicate LLVM static constructor registration
+    # (spirv-expand-step registered twice -> SIGABRT). The ln -f must be in the
+    # same RUN as the pip install so both files are in the same writable overlayfs
+    # layer. A separate RUN would copy-up instead of hardlink, leaving two inodes.
+    # Fix belongs in TheRock: rocm-sdk-devel should not ship its own comgr copy.
+    # See: https://amd-hub.atlassian.net/browse/AIMA-248
+    && ln -sf \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3 \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3
+ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+# Note: Primus uses `ROCM_HOME` instead of `ROCM_PATH`. Set both to avoid potential issues.
+ENV ROCM_HOME=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+ENV HIP_PLATFORM=amd
+ENV HIP_PATH=$ROCM_PATH
+ENV HIP_CLANG_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/llvm/bin
+ENV HIP_INCLUDE_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/include
+ENV HIP_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib
+ENV HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode
+ENV PATH="$ROCM_PATH/bin:$HIP_CLANG_PATH:$PATH"
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64:$ROCM_PATH/llvm/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib/host-math/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib/rocm_sysdeps/lib"
+ENV LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64"
+ENV CPATH=$HIP_INCLUDE_PATH
+ENV PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$ROCM_PATH/lib/pkgconfig"
+
+# Fix rocprofv3 issue with libamd_comgr.so.3 not found.
+# This is a workaround for the issue where rocprofv3 fails to find libamd_comgr.so.3
+# due to the way ROCm packages are structured. The workaround creates a symbolic link to
+# the correct location of libamd_comgr.so.3 and modifies the rocprofv3 script to avoid
+# calling update_env with True, which can cause issues in some environments.
+# See: https://amd-hub.atlassian.net/browse/AIMA-248
+RUN sed -i 's/update_env("ROCPROFILER_LIBRARY_CTOR", True)/update_env("ROCPROFILER_LIBRARY_CTOR", False)/' \
+  /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/bin/rocprofv3
+
+# Compile the numerically validated backward payload.
+# The hand-tuned forward asm override was retired upstream in Primus #1070's
+# simplified gpt-oss-20b recipe, so only the backward payload is built here.
+ARG BWD_ATTN_ASM_REPO=https://github.com/mawad-amd/bwd-attn-asm.git
+ARG BWD_ATTN_ASM_REF=9b9fb6444f3fee388617f62432c3faea74079377
+ARG BWD_ATTN_SOURCE_SYMBOL=_ZN5aiter43fmha_bwd_hd64_bf16_causal_a16_rtz_recompileE
+ARG BWD_ATTN_SYMBOL=_ZN5aiter44fmha_bwd_hd64_bf16_causal_a16_rtne_recompileE
+
+RUN git clone "${BWD_ATTN_ASM_REPO}" \
+    && cd bwd-attn-asm \
+    && git checkout "${BWD_ATTN_ASM_REF}" \
+    && sed "s/${BWD_ATTN_SOURCE_SYMBOL}/${BWD_ATTN_SYMBOL}/g" \
+      kernels/bwd_d64_v3_causal_opt_16x32.s > /tmp/bwd_attn.s \
+    && amdclang -x assembler -target amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -mcpu=gfx950 \
+      -o /tmp/bwd_attn.co /tmp/bwd_attn.s \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf bwd-attn-asm /tmp/bwd_attn.s
+
+# TransformerEngine
+ARG TE_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/TransformerEngine.git
+ARG TE_VERSION=023639b5168152a339e99d2e06c495dba26cf6cb
+ARG BWD_ATTN_SLOT=bwd_hd64_bf16_causal_a16_rtne.co
+
+ENV NVTE_USE_HIPBLASLT=1
+ENV NVTE_FRAMEWORK=pytorch
+ENV NVTE_ROCM_ARCH=${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}
+ENV NVTE_USE_CAST_TRANSPOSE_TRITON=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_IS_V3_ATOMIC_FP32=0
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_BWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_FWD_V3=1
+ENV CK_TILE_FLOAT_TO_BFLOAT16_DEFAULT=2
+ENV NVTE_CK_HOW_V3_BF16_CVT=2
+ENV NVTE_USE_ROCM=1
+
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_AOTRITON=0
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_CK=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_JIT=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_FUSED_ATTN_PATH=""
+ENV NVTE_AITER_SOURCE_DIR=/workspace/deps/te-aiter
+ENV NVTE_BUILD_MAX_JOBS="${MAX_JOBS}"
+ENV CU_NUM=304
+ENV NVTE_SKIP_SUBMODULE_CHECKS_DURING_BUILD=1
+ENV CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL="${MAX_JOBS}"
+
+RUN git clone --recursive ${TE_REPO} \
+    && cd TransformerEngine \
+    && git checkout ${TE_VERSION} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    # ROCm LLVM 24 lld (>= a20261004) treats the quoted typeinfo names in QoLA's
+    # version script as literals and errors when they match nothing; older lld
+    # silently ignored them, so dropping them keeps the exported symbols identical.
+    && sed -i '/"typeinfo for qola::\*";/d; /"typeinfo name for qola::\*";/d' \
+        3rdparty/QoLA/qola/cpp_itfs/qola_exports.lds \
+    && PYTHONPATH="$PWD/3rdparty/QoLA:${PYTHONPATH}" \
+        python3 -m qola.cli checkout \
+        --manifest transformer_engine/common/ck_fused_attn/qola_manifest.toml \
+        --aiter-root /workspace/deps/te-aiter \
+    && install -m 0644 /tmp/bwd_attn.co \
+        "/workspace/deps/te-aiter/hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/${BWD_ATTN_SLOT}" \
+    && uv pip install psutil \
+    && sed -i 's/hipFuncSetAttribute(/(void)hipFuncSetAttribute(/g' \
+        transformer_engine/common/gemm/kittens/cdna3/blockwise_fp8_gemm.cpp \
+    && printf '#include "../kittens_common.h"\nBlockwiseGemmBackend *BlockwiseGemmBackend::get_cdna4() { return nullptr; }\n' \
+        > transformer_engine/common/gemm/kittens/cdna4/blockwise_fp8_gemm.cpp \
+    # userbuffers-host.cpp pulls in util/cuda_nvml.h, which hipify rewrites to
+    # hip_nvml.h with `#include <rocm_smi/rocm_smi.h>` -- a header the rocm-sdk
+    # wheel doesn't ship, breaking the compile. NVML is only used by
+    # has_mnnvl_fabric(), whose sole NVML calls sit in the `#else` of
+    # `#if !defined(nvmlGpuFabricInfo_v2)`; on ROCm that macro is never defined,
+    # so the branch is compiled out and the include is dead. Drop it from the
+    # clone-time source (hipify then emits userbuffers-host_hip.cpp with no
+    # rocm_smi dependency). Patch the source, NOT the generated hip_nvml.h,
+    # which doesn't exist until `uv pip install .` runs hipify.
+    && sed -i '\|#include "common/util/cuda_nvml.h"|d' \
+        transformer_engine/common/comm_gemm_overlap/userbuffers/userbuffers-host.cpp \
+    && CXXFLAGS="-Wno-error=unused-value" \
+        HIPFLAGS="-Wno-error -Wno-unused-value" \
+        NVTE_BUILD_MAX_JOBS=${NVTE_BUILD_MAX_JOBS} \
+        MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS} \
+        CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=${CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL} \
+        uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf TransformerEngine te-aiter \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Flash Attention
+# ROCm/flash-attention tag v2.8.4.1-cktile, pinned to its commit for reproducibility
+# (a git tag is a movable pointer; the commit SHA is immutable). Bump both together.
+# Upstream PyPI flash-attn compiles the full combinatorial CK-tile FMHA instance set,
+# which OOM-kills a single splitkv_d64 TU at any -j; the fork's curated set builds clean.
+ARG FA_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/flash-attention.git
+ARG FA_REF=5301a359f59ef8fa10f211618d9f7a69716a8898
+RUN git clone --recursive ${FA_REPO} \
+    && cd flash-attention \
+    && git checkout ${FA_REF} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. && rm -rf flash-attention && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Flux
+ARG FLUX_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/AMDiffusionBenchmark.git
+ARG FLUX_BRANCH=26.4_RC_Patch_torchcodec
+
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/Diffusion_benchmark_patches.patch /workspace/Diffusion_benchmark_patches.patch
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/sdxl_patch.patch /workspace/sdxl_patch.patch
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/Diffusion_amd_smi.patch /workspace/Diffusion_amd_smi.patch
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/siheyuan-dataset-fix.patch /workspace/siheyuan-dataset-fix.patch
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/torchcodec_decord_video_shim.patch /workspace/torchcodec_decord_video_shim.patch
+
+# Cap huggingface-hub below 2: diffusers pulls it unbounded, and hub 2.x conflicts
+# with tokenizers (<2.0), so the later torchtune install can backtrack to
+# tokenizers 0.13.3, which has no cp312 wheel and fails to build without Rust.
+RUN git clone ${FLUX_REPO} \
+    && cd AMDiffusionBenchmark \
+    && git checkout ${FLUX_BRANCH} \
+    && uv pip install -r requirements.txt "huggingface-hub<2" \
+    && find . -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && git apply /workspace/Diffusion_benchmark_patches.patch \
+    && git apply /workspace/sdxl_patch.patch \
+    && git apply /workspace/Diffusion_amd_smi.patch \
+    && git apply /workspace/siheyuan-dataset-fix.patch \
+    && git apply /workspace/torchcodec_decord_video_shim.patch \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# DLRM
+ARG DLRM_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/DLRMBenchmark.git
+ARG DLRM_BRANCH=main
+
+RUN git clone ${DLRM_REPO} \
+    && cd DLRMBenchmark \
+    && git checkout ${DLRM_BRANCH} \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# torchtune
+ARG TORCHTUNE_REPO=https://github.com/pytorch/torchtune.git
+ARG TORCHTUNE_BRANCH=b4c98ac2a37f0397d64c22579aed415ce7264db6
+
+RUN git clone ${TORCHTUNE_REPO} \
+    && if [ "${TORCHTUNE_BRANCH}" != "" ]; then cd torchtune && git checkout ${TORCHTUNE_BRANCH} && cd ..; fi \
+    && cd torchtune \
+    && git checkout ${TORCHTUNE_BRANCH} \
+    && find torchtune/modules/moe/utils.py -type f -print0 | xargs -0 sed -i 's/use_grouped_mm = True/use_grouped_mm = False/g' \
+    && uv pip install . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf torchtune \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Note: we need to change `pad_inner_dim` default explicitly to address fp8 in torchtune issue
+# torchao
+ARG TORCHAO_REPO=https://github.com/pytorch/ao.git
+ARG TORCHAO_BRANCH=e9c7bead90b840b280f97374308255957108ce47
+
+RUN git clone ${TORCHAO_REPO} \
+    && cd ao && git checkout ${TORCHAO_BRANCH} \
+    && find torchao/float8/config.py -type f -print0 | xargs -0 sed -i 's/pad_inner_dim: bool = False/pad_inner_dim: bool = True/g' \
+    && find torchao/csrc/rocm/swizzle/swizzle.cpp -type f -print0 | xargs -0 sed -i 's/if defined(HIPBLASLT_VEC_EXT)/if false/g' \
+    && uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf ao \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+RUN uv pip install \
+    datasets==5.0.1 \
+    av==16.0.1 \
+    transformers==5.10.0 \
+    optree==0.18.0 \
+    sympy==1.14.0 \
+    accelerate==1.9.0 \
+    trl==0.21.0 \
+    tensorboard==2.20.0 \
+    peft \
+    scipy \
+    einops \
+    flask-restful \
+    nltk \
+    pytest \
+    pytest-cov \
+    pytest_mock \
+    pytest-csv \
+    pytest-random-order \
+    sentencepiece \
+    wrapt \
+    zarr==2.18.7 \
+    numcodecs==0.12.1 \
+    xarray \
+    wandb==0.28.2 \
+    tensorstore==0.1.45 \
+    pytest_mock \
+    pybind11 \
+    tiktoken \
+    pynvml \
+    huggingface_hub[cli] \
+    && python3 -m nltk.downloader punkt_tab \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Groupped GEMM
+ARG GROUPED_GEMM_REPO=https://github.com/caaatch22/grouped_gemm.git
+ARG GROUPED_GEMM_BRANCH=rocm
+
+RUN git clone ${GROUPED_GEMM_REPO} \
+    && cd grouped_gemm \
+    && git checkout ${GROUPED_GEMM_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/g' setup.py \
+    && uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf grouped_gemm \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Install Causal-Conv1d and its dependencies
+ARG CAUSAL_CONV1D_REPO=https://github.com/Dao-AILab/causal-conv1d
+ARG CAUSAL_CONV1D_BRANCH=e940ead2fd962c56854455017541384909ca669f
+
+ENV CAUSAL_CONV1D_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE
+ENV MAMBA_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE
+ENV HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx942,gfx950
+
+RUN git clone ${CAUSAL_CONV1D_REPO} causal-conv1d \
+    && cd causal-conv1d \
+    && git checkout ${CAUSAL_CONV1D_BRANCH} \
+    && git show --oneline -s \
+    && sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/g' setup.py \
+    && uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -fr causal-conv1d \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Mamba
+ARG MAMBA_REPO=https://github.com/AndreasKaratzas/mamba.git
+ARG MAMBA_BRANCH=enable-primus-hybrid-models
+
+# The last two sed patches below drop the complex-valued selective_scan backward
+# kernels. The ROCm/TheRock LLVM (clang/lld 24.0git) crashes with
+# "LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: f32 = Constant<-1>" during AMDGPU instruction
+# selection when LTO-linking selective_scan_bwd_*_complex for gfx942/gfx950.
+# Real-valued Mamba/Mamba-2 SSMs never use a complex A matrix, so these kernels
+# are unreachable. We also delete the ComplexFloat branch from the shared
+# dispatch macro so the backward path emits no undefined reference under
+# `ld.lld --no-undefined`.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11 \
+        nvidia-cuda-nvdisasm==13.3.73 \
+    && git clone --branch ${MAMBA_BRANCH} ${MAMBA_REPO} \
+    && cd mamba \
+    && sed -i '/^\s*namespace std\s*=\s*::std\s*;/d' csrc/selective_scan/uninitialized_copy.cuh \
+    && sed -i '/namespace cuda {/,/^    }/{/namespace cuda {/d;/namespace std = ::std;/d;/^    }$/d;}' csrc/selective_scan/uninitialized_copy.cuh \
+    && sed -i 's/::cuda::std::/::std::/g' csrc/selective_scan/uninitialized_copy.cuh \
+    && sed -i '/selective_scan_bwd_fp32_complex\.cu/d;/selective_scan_bwd_fp16_complex\.cu/d;/selective_scan_bwd_bf16_complex\.cu/d' setup.py \
+    && sed -i '/} else if (WTYPE == at::ScalarType::ComplexFloat) {/,+2d' csrc/selective_scan/selective_scan.cpp \
+    && sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/g' setup.py \
+    && python setup.py install \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Primus
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus.git
+# Latest commit on `release/v26.9` branch. Commited on 2026-10-30.
+ARG PRIMUS_BRANCH=db1a41601833294231daadb3cdbb2933eb805c73
+# Note: those envs are required to resolve ther issue around the primus update
+# post v26.2
+ENV NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
+ENV PRIMUS_FLA_MLA_ATTN=1
+
+# multi-storage-client (via megatron-energon in Primus's requirements) caps filelock<4,
+# which would pull it back off 4.2.1 (CVE-2026-112940, fixed only in 4.x). It only uses
+# FileLock/BaseFileLock/Timeout, which 4.x still provides, so override the cap.
+RUN git clone --recurse-submodules ${PRIMUS_REPO} \
+    && cd Primus \
+    && git checkout ${PRIMUS_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && echo "filelock==4.2.1" > /tmp/overrides.txt \
+    && uv pip install --override /tmp/overrides.txt -r requirements.txt \
+    && find . -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /tmp/overrides.txt /root/.cache /tmp/bwd_attn.co
+
+# Aiter
+# The pinned commit below is kept current by the nightly sweep, which resolves it to
+# the latest aiter GitHub release: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/releases
+ARG AITER_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git
+ARG AITER_COMMIT=778d74d57c765616ee36a0c3295dc446e5027d5f
+
+RUN uv pip uninstall aiter amd-aiter \
+    && rm -rf aiter \
+    && git clone --recursive ${AITER_REPO} \
+    && cd aiter \
+    && git checkout ${AITER_COMMIT} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && PREBUILD_KERNELS=3 uv pip install --no-cache . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf aiter \
+    && find /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aiter_meta -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete
+
+# Primus-Turbo
+ARG TURBO_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo.git
+# Latest commit on `main` branch. Commited on 2026-10-19.
+ARG TURBO_COMMIT=de8fa6ca7f4986334070d5ee62beee07552f8ad8
+ENV HCC_AMDGPU_TARGET="gfx942,gfx950"
+ENV PRIMUS_TURBO_FRAMEWORK=PYTORCH
+
+RUN git clone ${TURBO_REPO} --recursive \
+    && cd Primus-Turbo \
+    && git checkout ${TURBO_COMMIT} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    # Triton 3.9 rejects autotune keys that are not kernel arguments; older Triton
+    # silently dropped them. The bwd kernels take BLOCK_DMODEL_QK/_V, so the stale
+    # "BLOCK_DMODEL" key is removed (same effective key as before).
+    && { [ ! -f primus_turbo/triton/attention/attention_kernel.py ] \
+         || sed -i '/^        "BLOCK_DMODEL",$/d' primus_turbo/triton/attention/attention_kernel.py; } \
+    && uv pip install -r requirements.txt \
+    && uv pip install --no-build-isolation . -v \
+        --extra-index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --extra-index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+    && find . -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# fla 0.5.2 lists a stale "BT" autotune key on merge_fwd_bwd_kernel (not a kernel
+# argument), which Triton 3.9 rejects at import. Fixed upstream in fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1330
+# but unreleased; this is a no-op once a release includes it.
+RUN f=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/fla/ops/cp/chunk_delta_h.py \
+    && { [ ! -f "$f" ] || sed -i "s/key=\['HV', 'K', 'V', 'BT'\]/key=['HV', 'K', 'V']/" "$f"; }
+
+RUN uv pip install \
+    boto3==1.35.42 \
+    botocore==1.35.99 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Force-upgrade transitive deps pulled in by the packages above to pick up CVE fixes.
+# cryptography is bumped past 48.0.1 for CVE-2026-69247/CVE-2026-69249 (Trivy),
+# both disclosed after that pin was first set. CVE-2026-69247 is fixed only in
+# cryptography 50.0.0, so this pin cannot move down.
+# hydra-core is bumped to 1.3.8 to fix code-execution flaws in hydra.utils.instantiate,
+# CVE-2026-106439/CVE-2026-106441/CVE-2026-106442 and GHSA-wf6j-7hvr-gr93 (Trivy).
+RUN uv pip install \
+    cryptography==50.0.0 \
+    diffusers==0.38.0 \
+    hydra-core==1.3.8 \
+    jaraco.context==6.1.0 \
+    pyarrow==23.0.1 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# mlflow is pulled in transitively by Primus's requirements.txt (installed above)
+# at an older, CVE-affected version; force the fixed 3.17.2 release (CVE-2026-53995
+# HIGH; also covers CVE-2026-64849 CRITICAL, CVE-2026-8147 HIGH). Installed with
+# --no-deps because mlflow caps cryptography<50, which would otherwise drag the pin
+# above off 50.0.0 and undo the CVE-2026-69247 fix. mlflow's cryptography<50 bound is
+# conservative, not a real incompatibility, and its other runtime deps are already
+# satisfied by the earlier requirements.txt install. mlflow pins mlflow-skinny and
+# mlflow-tracing to its own version, so install those alongside it.
+RUN uv pip install --no-deps mlflow==3.17.2 mlflow-skinny==3.17.2 mlflow-tracing==3.17.2 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+WORKDIR /workspace/
+
+# Install torchrec
+RUN uv pip install --no-deps torchrec \
+    && uv pip install \
+        tensordict \
+        iopath \
+        torchmetrics==1.0.3 \
+        git+https://github.com/mlperf/logging.git \
+        --extra-index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --extra-index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Install FBGEMM
+ARG FBGEMM_REPO=https://github.com/pytorch/FBGEMM.git
+# Latest known working commit on the `main` branch. Committed on 2026-06-17.
+ARG FBGEMM_COMMIT=80bd3c077dc41b55cd16ed4dcad15cf7c1c1d76a
+ENV BUILD_ROCM_VERSION='7.15'
+
+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y libtbb-dev \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+RUN git clone ${FBGEMM_REPO} \
+    && cd FBGEMM \
+    && git checkout ${FBGEMM_COMMIT} \
+    && cd fbgemm_gpu \
+    && git clean -dfx \
+    && git submodule sync \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && sed -i 's/-Wno-error=attributes)/-Wno-error=attributes\n    -Wno-error=unused-value)/' ../cmake/modules/CppLibrary.cmake \
+    && sed -i 's/-Wno-unused-result)/-Wno-unused-result\n    -Wno-unused-value)/' ../cmake/modules/RocmSetup.cmake \
+    && sed -i 's/cub::CTA_SYNC()/__syncthreads()/g' src/sparse_ops/sparse_async_batched_cumsum.cu \

+    && uv pip install setuptools==80.10.2 \
+    && python setup.py install \

+        --build-target=default \

+        -DHIP_ROOT_DIR=$ROCM_PATH \
+        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DTORCH_USE_HIP_DSA -Wno-unused-value" \
+        -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-DTORCH_USE_HIP_DSA -Wno-unused-value" \
+    && cd .. \
+    && find external/composable_kernel -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \

+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y numactl \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y \

+    jq \
+    dpkg-dev \

+    infiniband-diags \
+    rdma-core \
+    ethtool \
+    libevent-dev \
+    libhwloc-dev \
+    libmunge-dev \

+    && apt update --allow-insecure-repositories \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y --allow-unauthenticated libionic-dev libionic1 \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+

+
+# Install UCX
+ARG UCX_VERSION="1.18.0"
+
+RUN wget https://github.com/openucx/ucx/releases/download/v${UCX_VERSION}/ucx-${UCX_VERSION}.tar.gz \
+    && mkdir -p ucx-${UCX_VERSION} \
+    && tar -zxf ucx-${UCX_VERSION}.tar.gz -C ucx-${UCX_VERSION} --strip-components=1 \
+    && cd ucx-${UCX_VERSION} \
+    && mkdir build \
+    && cd build \
+    && ../configure --prefix=/workspace/ucx-${UCX_VERSION}/install --with-rocm=${ROCM_PATH} \
+    && make -j 16 \
+    && make install \
+    && cd ../.. \
+    && rm ucx-${UCX_VERSION}.tar.gz
+
+ENV UCX_INSTALL_DIR=/workspace/ucx-${UCX_VERSION}/install
+
+# Install OpenMPI
+ARG MPI_VERSION="4.1.6"
+
+RUN wget https://download.open-mpi.org/release/open-mpi/v$(echo "${MPI_VERSION}" | cut -d. -f1-2)/openmpi-${MPI_VERSION}.tar.gz \
+    && mkdir -p ompi-${MPI_VERSION} \
+    && tar -zxf openmpi-${MPI_VERSION}.tar.gz -C ompi-${MPI_VERSION} --strip-components=1 \
+    && cd ompi-${MPI_VERSION} \
+    && mkdir build \
+    && cd build \
+    && ../configure --prefix=/opt/openmpi --with-ucx=${UCX_INSTALL_DIR} --disable-oshmem --disable-mpi-fortran \
+    && make -j 16 \
+    && make install \
+    && cd ../.. \
+    && rm openmpi-${MPI_VERSION}.tar.gz \
+    && rm -rf ompi-${MPI_VERSION}

+ENV PATH="/opt/openmpi/bin:${PATH}"
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/openmpi/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
+

+
+# MLPerf related changes
+ARG MLPERF_COMMENT_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/mlperf-common.git
+# Latest commit on `main` branch. Commited on 2026-10-05 (merge of PR #3, MLPerf 6.1
+# precision events). Primus >= #1223 passes lowest_numerical_precision_in_{linear,attn,comm}
+# to this package, so it must stay at or after this commit.
+ARG MLPERF_COMMENT_COMMIT=7771aeabc8b91402e95cb7a33f447d9d9941361f
+
+RUN uv pip install git+${MLPERF_COMMENT_REPO}@${MLPERF_COMMENT_COMMIT} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Overwrite the wandb-core binary with the CVE-patched rebuild from the
+# wandb_core_builder stage. This MUST come after every `pip install` above:
+# Primus's requirements.txt (and others) pull in the wandb wheel, which would
+# otherwise reinstate the stock vulnerable binary at this path. The wandb pip
+# pin (wandb==0.28.2) and the builder's WANDB_VERSION (v0.28.2) must be kept in
+# sync so the Python package matches the rebuilt binary's source tag.
+COPY --from=wandb_core_builder /wandb-core /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/wandb/bin/wandb-core
+
+# Some secrets could leak from these files. Explicitly clean them out.
+RUN rm -f /workspace/Megatron-LM/.gitlab/stages/00.pre.yml \
+ /workspace/Primus/third_party/Megatron-LM/.gitlab/stages/00.pre.yml
+
+# Secret scan will complain those files to be secrets. Explicitly remove them.
+RUN rm -f /workspace/Primus/.git/packed-refs /workspace/Primus/.git/modules/third_party/**/packed-refs
+
+# Clean cache
+RUN rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Clean build files
+RUN rm -rf /*.whl \
+    && rm -rf /root/.triton \
+    && rm -rf /workspace/aiter/aiter/jit/build \
+    && rm -rf /workspace/TransformerEngine
+
+# Note: this image intentionally runs as root (no USER instruction). Training
+# workloads here need direct access to GPU and AINIC devices, which requires root
+# privileges. Accepted risk.
+
+# Strip example/dev Dockerfiles that ship inside the composable_kernel submodule
+# source tree baked into the base image (under /workspace/deps/te-aiter). They are
+# never invoked by this image -- only the compiled CK libraries are used at runtime
+# -- but Trivy's misconfig scanner flags them (DS-0010 sudo, DS-0031 secret env, etc.
+# as CRITICAL). Deleting only the Dockerfile* files clears those findings with no
+# effect on the CK build artifacts. Guarded so a base image without this tree is a no-op.
+RUN if [ -d /workspace/deps/te-aiter ]; then \
+        find /workspace/deps/te-aiter -name 'Dockerfile*' -type f -delete; \
+    fi
+
+# Training docker manifest
+ARG GIT_COMMIT_TAG=DEV
+ARG DOCKERFILE_PATH=Dockerfile
+
+# Copy patch files for training docker versioning
+RUN mkdir -p /workspace/.manifest \
+    && env > /workspace/.manifest/env.txt \
+    && uv pip list > /workspace/.manifest/requirements.txt \
+    && dpkg -l > /workspace/.manifest/dpkg-list.txt \
+    && echo "${GIT_COMMIT_TAG}" > /workspace/.manifest/training_docker_version
+
+COPY ${DOCKERFILE_PATH} /workspace/.manifest/docker-build-recipe.txt
+
+CMD ["/usr/bin/bash"]

+**Both families move to ROCm nightlies.** `rocm/primus` moves from the ROCm 10.1.0 release to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20261020`), with a PyTorch 2.16 pre-release and a Transformer Engine 2.20 development build, still built from source. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.3 nightly (`10.3.0a20261026`) with JAX 0.12.0, a Transformer Engine 2.19 development build, and MaxText `release/v26.9`, and **ships a copy of Primus again**. Both images were built from the same Primus commit, `db1a4160` on `release/v26.9`—see [Primus source for v26.9](#primus-source-for-v269).
 
 ### Both families
 
+- **A convergence test for Megatron and MaxText.** `tools/convergence_test/` builds a dataset from a real corpus, lints the config for settings that silently spoil a convergence run (mock or synthetic data, forced load balancing, vocab mismatches), trains through the normal `primus-cli` path, plots the loss, and gates it against a previous release's baseline ([#1229](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1229)). It ships Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-2-7B, and Mixtral-8x7B recipes for both backends, plus a MaxText Llama-2-7B FP8 recipe for MI355X ([#1261](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1261)).
+- **The `tools/perf` batch runner is ready for unattended runs.** Each run is bounded by `MAX_RUN_SECONDS` (default 1 h) and `MAX_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 20 min); busy GPUs and bad network interfaces are refused up front; failures are classified with the log line that shows them; every result records the image, host, and platform it came from; diffusion and DLRM benchmarks join the batch; and results go into an Excel report that can compare against a baseline ([#1260](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1260), [#1266](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1266), [#1299](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1299)). Two misreported throughput values are fixed: TorchTitan values printed with a thousands separator, and Megatron-Bridge's post-training estimate. Note the behavior changes: single-node runs now time out, output files have fixed names, and the runners exit non-zero when any run fails.
+- **Release benchmark suites in the auto-benchmark menu.** One choice detects the GPU and runs the whole Primus suite (Megatron, Megatron Bridge, TorchTitan) or JAX suite (MaxText, MaxDiffusion), recording the image digest, Primus commit, and submodule pins with every result ([#1251](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1251)).
+- **A preset `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is kept.** The runner used to overwrite it with `0..GPUS_PER_NODE-1`, so on a shared node a job could land on another user's GPU; it now keeps your selection and warns when its count differs from `GPUS_PER_NODE` ([#1237](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1237)).
+
+### `rocm/primus`: Megatron-LM and TorchTitan
+
+#### Changes you might need to act on
+
+- **Mock-data runs use the model's real vocabulary.** Megatron mock data used to size every model for a 131,072-token vocabulary; each model config now sets its real `vocab_size`, so embeddings, output layer, and logits have their true size. Mock-data throughput and memory are therefore not comparable with earlier releases ([#1249](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1249)).
+- **Megatron-only example material moved under `examples/megatron/`.** For example `examples/deepseek-v4/` is now `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/`, and `examples/moe_package/` is now `examples/megatron/guides/moe_package/`; `examples/mlperf/` and `examples/hardware_configs/` stay where they were. Update scripts that name the old paths ([#1130](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1130)).
+- **Some environment switches are now config keys, and the old variables do nothing.** `PRIMUS_FUSED_QK_RMSNORM_ROPE` is replaced by `use_turbo_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope` ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)); `PRIMUS_TURBO_CROSS_ENTROPY` and `PRIMUS_TURBO_CE_OVERWRITE_INPUT` by `use_turbo_cross_entropy` and `turbo_ce_overwrite_input` ([#1245](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1245)); the MoE gather-quantization variables by `moe_permute_quant_fusion`, `moe_backward_permute_quant_fusion`, and `moe_skip_identity_sort` ([#1241](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1241)).
+- **Transformer Engine fused cross entropy reuses the logits buffer by default** (`te_ce_overwrite_input: true`), so after the loss backward the logits tensor holds its gradient. Set it to `false` when the same logits feed anything else in the step, such as a distillation or auxiliary loss, metrics, or hooks ([#1287](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1287)).
+- **TorchTitan uses a Triton fused AdamW by default** (`optimizer.use_triton_fused_adam: true`). Checkpoints stay interchangeable with `torch.optim.AdamW`; set the flag to `false` to go back to it. Reading `optimizer.state` directly between steps now shows stale `step` values ([#1233](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1233)).
+- **Turbo grouped GEMM expects expandable segments.** Primus warns when `use_turbo_grouped_gemm` is on without `expandable_segments:True`, and a runner hook stops the launch when `expandable_segments:True` is requested but not in effect on the PyTorch build ([#1257](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1257)).
+
+#### New features
+
+- **GLM-5.3-Flash** (`model_type: glm5_next`): KDA linear attention, DSA sparse attention, and manifold-constrained hyper-connections with a 288-expert MoE, an MI355X BF16 recipe, and online loading of the released Hugging Face checkpoint for any TP / EP / PP layout ([#1230](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1230)). Packed sequences now run under context parallelism ([#1265](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1265)) and text-only checkpoint exports load ([#1254](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1254)). Training was validated on an 8-layer proxy; the full 45-layer model was checked forward-only against SGLang, and its DSA indexer is frozen.
+- **ZAYA1-8B FP8 recipes** for MI300X, MI325X, and MI355X (`fp8: hybrid`, tensorwise scaling, accurate from a cold start) and an MI325X BF16 recipe ([#1269](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1269)); the MI355X micro-batch sizes now fill that GPU's memory ([#1279](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1279)).
+- **HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training**, stage 1 (geometry heads) and stage 2 (Gaussian head), with MI355X configs launched through `train posttrain`. The upstream trainer is the new `third_party/HunyuanWorld-Mirror-rocm` submodule; Primus applies ROCm fixes at runtime ([#1242](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1242)).
+- **MiniMax-M3 on MegaMoE.** The fused MegaMoE expert layer accepts MiniMax-M3's `swigluoai` activation and matches the DeepEP path's loss ([#1243](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1243)).
+- **Opt-in fusions:** Primus-Turbo fused cross entropy for TP1 training ([#1245](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1245)); FlyDSL Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE and residual RMSNorm + MXFP4 QKV fusions for GPT-OSS ([#1208](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1208)), with the fused Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE now also covering head dimension 128 ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)); and gradient reduce-scatter on the GPU's copy engines (`MEGATRON_GRAD_REDUCE_BACKEND=rccl_sdma`, which needs an RCCL build with CE ReduceScatter) ([#1207](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1207)).
+- **gfx1250 FP8 hybrid LoRA SFT proxies** for Llama-2-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, and Qwen3-235B-A22B on one GPU ([#1248](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1248)).
+
+#### Performance
+
+- **Optimizer and MoE kernel work, opt-in:** gradient clipping and BF16 Adam moments fused into the Adam update ([#1219](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1219)), fused MXFP4 weight de-oscillation ([#1222](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1222)), BF16 router backward GEMMs (`moe_router_bwd_bf16`, [#1240](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1240)), and MoE gathers folded into Primus-Turbo MXFP4 quantization ([#1241](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1241)).
+- **Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 on MI355X** moves to Primus-Turbo tensorwise FP8 with the Turbo grouped-MLP, activation, and permute fusions ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)).
+- **Tuned configs:** MI355X GPT-OSS-20B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Llama 70B, Qwen, Mixtral, and TorchTitan Llama recipes ([#1218](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1218), [#1252](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1252), [#1349](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1349)); MI300X GPT-OSS-20B and Llama 70B ([#1307](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1307), [#1332](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1332), [#1304](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1304)); MI325X Llama 70B and ZAYA1-8B ([#1318](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1318)). Two of these change more than speed: MI355X DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16 now uses MLA, the model's real attention, and MI355X GPT-OSS-20B FP8 trains with global batch 96 instead of 80 ([#1252](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1252)).
+
+#### Bug fixes
+
+- **Stale expert weights with the fused grouped MLP.** With `turbo_fused_grouped_gemm` and `overlap_param_gather`, the fused op skipped the hooks that wait for the expert-weight all-gather, so whenever expert data parallelism exceeded one it read partly stale weights: no error and no NaN, just a drifting loss ([#1252](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1252)).
+- **Forced "even" routing under DeepEP.** With DeepEP on, most routed slots received weight 0 and the MoE output collapsed toward the shared expert; the router now does the remap itself ([#1243](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1243)).
+- **MoE recipes no longer force the DeepEP cheap fence.** v26.8 recipes set `PRIMUS_TURBO_DEEPEP_DISABLE_CHEAP_FENCE=0`, which could corrupt DeepEP dispatch-backward rows; the variable is removed from the 13 MI355X and MI325X recipes that set it ([#1236](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1236)).
+- **MoE models no longer hang on hosts with an amdgpu DRM interface older than 3.64.** A runner hook detects such hosts and keeps HIP memory pools off virtual-memory mappings ([#1302](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1302)).
+- **DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connections** contract on the same axis as the inference kernels; the old convention drifted from SGLang by more with every layer ([#1040](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1040)).
+- **TorchTitan:** DeepSeek blocks are compiled inside their activation-checkpoint wrappers, so with full checkpointing the MoE block no longer runs eagerly ([#1320](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1320)); and the Primus-Turbo attention converter applies only when both `enable_primus_turbo` and `use_turbo_attention` are on, fixing a `TypeError` on the first forward otherwise ([#1234](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1234)).
+- Smaller fixes: the Turbo FP8 weight cache is stored in the operator's padded layout ([#1333](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1333)), and `enable_turbo_attention_float8` no longer fails on its first call ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)).
+
+### `rocm/jax-training:maxtext`: MaxText
+
+- **The image ships Primus again.** `/workspace/Primus` is at `db1a4160`, the commit the image was built from; a `release/v26.9` checkout is still recommended—see [Primus source for v26.9](#primus-source-for-v269).
+- **MaxText moves to `release/v26.9`** (`8d1d43c0`), carrying the same ROCm patches as v26.8 on newer upstream. Upstream drops the `retry_when_tokens_dropped` config key, so remove it from any local config, and renames the `cosmos3-*-reasoner` model configs to `weaver-max` / `weaver-mini` ([#1316](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1316)).
+- **XLA autotuning defaults to level 3.** At Primus's previous default, level 4, the autotuner's correctness checks intermittently aborted compilation of the train step on GPU 0; level 3 keeps autotuning and drops only those checks. Set `XLA_GPU_AUTOTUNE_LEVEL=4` to restore the old default ([#1316](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1316)).
+- **Transformer Engine's per-call `return_max_logit` warning is silenced.** It was printed on every backward attention call, per layer, per GPU, and per step; Primus now passes the same fallback value TE was using, so numerics are unchanged ([#1316](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1316)).
+- **MaxText runs on real data no longer stop before the first step.** Grain data-loader workers read absl flags that Primus had left unparsed, and MaxText reported the error as a graceful stop: zero steps trained, exit status 0. Synthetic-data runs, including the benchmark configs, were not affected ([#1229](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1229)).
+- **Recipe fixes:** the MI300X Wan2.1-1.3B and MI355X Mixtral-8x7B FP8 out-of-memory errors are fixed, and FLUX.1-dev is retuned on MI300X and MI355X ([#1338](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1338), [#1349](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1349)).
+- **Primus Projection gains a MaxText/JAX backend** ([#1232](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1232)). Its benchmark path has so far been verified on CPU only.

+### Highlights for v26.8
+
+**The two families split on ROCm.** `rocm/primus` moves to the ROCm 10.1.0 release with PyTorch 2.14, and builds Transformer Engine and Flash Attention from source again. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20260923`) with JAX 0.11.1 and a Transformer Engine 2.18 development build, and **no longer ships a copy of Primus**: run it with a `release/v26.8` checkout, which `primus-cli container` mounts for you. Bare-metal installs changed accordingly — see [Bare-metal installation](./bare-metal-installation.md) and the [JAX guide](./bare-metal-installation-jax.md).
+
+#### Both families
+

-## 6. Notes
-
-- **1 GPU:** `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`, `GPUS_PER_NODE=1`. `MI455X.sh` then sets
-  `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` and `AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=0`.
-- **Do not** set `AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=3`.
-- Proxies still download a **tokenizer** (Llama-2-7B tokenizer, Qwen2.5-0.5B,
-  or Qwen3-0.6B) and **Alpaca**. They do not download the 70B/72B/235B weights.
-- Qwen3 MoE: `use_turbo_deepep: false` (DeepEP CPU recv timeout on this box).
-  LoRA targets are attention only; do not add `linear_fc1` / `linear_fc2` or
-  LoRA hits `PrimusTurboColumnParallelGroupedLinear` and raises
-  `NotImplementedError`.
-- If Gloo dies with `Unable to find address for: <ip>`, the image is missing
-  `iproute2` or you sourced `MI455X.sh` without `primus-env.sh`.

**2. 🟠 Should fix: Installation README says apex must match torch's ROCm, contradicting the new ROCm 10.3 apex pin**

The 'Index contents move' caveat in `tools/installation/README.md` (~line 292) still says `apex` must target the same ROCm version as `torch`/`rocm-sdk-*`. That contradicts the new pin `APEX_VERSION=1.16.0a0+rocm10.3.0a20261029` next to the 10.2.0a20261020 set. The same README (line 89) and `setup.sh` already explain that this is the build the v26.9 image itself resolved. Drop `apex` from that list and note it as the image's exception, as the PR already does in the other doc that carries this caveat.

**Who is affected:** Bare-metal installers who update the setup.sh pin block after a pin stops resolving.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**3. 🟠 Should fix: JAX image's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` comment describes TE 2.17, `jax_rocm7_plugin` and a nonexistent RCCL override**

The comment above `ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=""` was copied unchanged from the v26.7/v26.8 Dockerfiles. It still names 'TE 2.17', `jax_rocm7_plugin` and an 'in-place RCCL override in jax_base'. This image installs TE `2.19.0.dev0` and the `jax_rocm10_{pjrt,plugin}` 0.12.0 wheels, and has no in-place RCCL override. The ENV also sits before the JAX/TE installs, not 'after every build step'. Update the comment; it does not change the built image.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers debugging the double-ROCm-runtime segfault in the v26.9 JAX image.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

+# directly in --from.

+FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv_bin

+# golang.org/x/net versions with known CVEs; bump them explicitly since no newer

+# `go get`: as an indirect dep its require floor gets pulled back below the fix by
+# `go mod tidy`/MVS (observed drift to v0.54.0), while replace pins the build to
+# exactly v0.55.0. x/net is pinned exact (not -u) for the same drift reason.

+    && cd /src \
+    && go get -u golang.org/x/sys \
+    && go get golang.org/x/net@v0.56.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/crypto=golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 \
+    && go mod tidy \
+    && go build -o /bazelisk
+
+# transformer_engine_rocm_jax's own build vendors a copy of GoogleCloudPlatform/gcsfuse
+# (built to /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse) whose go.mod pins golang.org/x/text,
+# golang.org/x/net and google.golang.org/grpc versions with known CVEs; this isn't
+# fixed upstream as of gcsfuse's latest release, so rebuild the same binaries here
+# with those deps bumped and overwrite whatever TE's build (and later, MaxText's
+# apt-installed gcsfuse package) produced, preserving identical behavior. Both the
+# main gcsfuse binary and the mount.gcsfuse helper embed these deps, so both are
+# rebuilt. x/crypto and grpc use `replace` directives to force the CVE-fixed
+# versions past gcsfuse's own go.mod pins.

+ARG GCSFUSE_VERSION=v3.11.2
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${GCSFUSE_VERSION} https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcsfuse.git /src \
+    && cd /src \
+    && go get golang.org/x/text@v0.39.0 \
+    && go get golang.org/x/net@v0.60.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace google.golang.org/grpc=google.golang.org/grpc@v1.83.2 \
+    && go mod edit -replace golang.org/x/crypto=golang.org/x/crypto@v0.57.0 \
+    && go mod edit -replace github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4=github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4@v4.1.6 \
+    && go mod tidy \
+    && go build -o /mount.gcsfuse ./tools/mount_gcsfuse \
+    && go build -o /gcsfuse .

+# pip's vendored msgpack, setuptools and urllib3 are flagged by Trivy via pip's SBOM
+# (pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json): GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964, CVE-2025-47273, CVE-2026-97687/97689.
+# Rebuild pip with msgpack 1.2.3, urllib3 2.8.0 and setuptools 79.0.1 (highest that
+# satisfies pip's `setuptools<80` vendor pin) so the regenerated SBOM is clean.

+ARG PIP_VERSION=26.2.2

+# from sdist and needs a C compiler; the compiled .so is dropped afterward per
+# pip's own vendoring config, leaving the pure-Python copy pip ships.

+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \

+        -e 's/^msgpack==.*/msgpack==1.2.3/' \
+        -e 's/^setuptools==.*/setuptools==79.0.1/' \

+	ninja-build \
+	g++ \
+	pkg-config \
+	xxd \
+	patchelf \
+	automake \
+	libtool \
+	python3-venv \

+	python-is-python3 \

+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3

+ENV ROCM_HOME=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel

+ENV HIP_PATH=$ROCM_PATH
+ENV HIP_CLANG_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/llvm/bin
+ENV HIP_INCLUDE_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/include
+ENV HIP_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib
+ENV HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode
+ENV PATH="$ROCM_PATH/bin:$HIP_CLANG_PATH:$PATH"
+ENV LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64"
+ENV CPATH=$HIP_INCLUDE_PATH
+ENV PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$ROCM_PATH/lib/pkgconfig"

**4. 🟠 Should fix: Parity `--check` reports torchvision/torchaudio drift as OK: this PR files identical pins as documented divergences**

`TORCHVISION_VERSION` and `TORCHAUDIO_VERSION` are now described in `documented_divergences.primus` as inline pins of the same version, not divergences. `compare()` puts any documented name with no Dockerfile counterpart into the divergent bucket without comparing values, so future drift on these pins would be reported as deliberate. The torchaudio entry, the empty `inline_pins.primus` and the `_comment` citing `Dockerfile.primus-v26.6` were already like this on the base. The torchvision entry is the one this PR changed from a real divergence. Moving them to `inline_pins` only helps if `${THE_ROCK_VERSION}` is substituted or the pattern captures only the literal part of the version: `inline_pins()` returns the raw capture, which would then show false drift against the script's literal value.

**Who is affected:** Release maintainers relying on `install_parity.py --check` to catch torch companion-wheel drift between `Dockerfile.primus-v26.9` and `tools/installation/setup.sh`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**5. 🟠 Should fix: JAX image build fetches full clones of unused PyTorch submodules: this PR restored `--recurse-submodules` clone**

The Primus layer in `Dockerfile.jax-v26.9` runs `git clone --recurse-submodules`. That fetches full, non-shallow clones of all 10 submodules in `.gitmodules` at the default-branch pins, before `git checkout ${PRIMUS_BRANCH}`. The layer then re-initialises only `third_party/maxtext`. The image uses its own `/workspace/maxtext` through `MAXTEXT_PATH`, so the PyTorch-backend submodules (Megatron-LM, torchtitan, Megatron-Bridge, Automodel, ...) are dead weight that costs build time and image size. The block is copied unchanged from `Dockerfile.jax-v26.4` through `v26.7`. A plain clone followed by a shallow `git submodule update --init --depth 1 third_party/maxtext` would avoid the cost.

**Who is affected:** Anyone building the v26.9 JAX release image; it costs build time and image size, and the image still works.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next/rocm/
+ENV THE_ROCK_VERSION=10.3.0a20261026
+
+# Note: we need to ensure all the ROCm packages are installed with the same version to avoid
+# potential issues. However, right now during the nightly sweep we only look at the latest version
+# rocm. If we ever run into issues, we can consider sweeping all the ROCm packages and pinning them
+# to a common latest version.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --pre \
+        rocm==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-bootstrap \
+        rocm-sdk-core==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-devel==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx942==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx950==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-libraries==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+RUN rocm-sdk init \
+    # Workaround: rocm-sdk-core and rocm-sdk-devel both ship libamd_comgr.so.3
+    # as separate inodes, causing duplicate LLVM static constructor registration
+    # (spirv-expand-step registered twice -> SIGABRT). The ln -f must be in the
+    # same RUN as the pip install so both files are in the same writable overlayfs
+    # layer. A separate RUN would copy-up instead of hardlink, leaving two inodes.
+    # Fix belongs in TheRock: rocm-sdk-devel should not ship its own comgr copy.
+    # See: https://amd-hub.atlassian.net/browse/AIMA-248
+    && ln -sf \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3 \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3
+COPY --from=bazelisk_builder /bazelisk /usr/local/bin/bazel
+ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+# Note: Primus uses `ROCM_HOME` instead of `ROCM_PATH`. Set both to avoid potential issues.
+ENV ROCM_HOME=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+ENV HIP_PLATFORM=amd
+ENV HIP_PATH=$ROCM_PATH
+ENV HIP_CLANG_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/llvm/bin
+ENV HIP_INCLUDE_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/include
+ENV HIP_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib
+ENV HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode
+ENV PATH="$ROCM_PATH/bin:$HIP_CLANG_PATH:$PATH"
+ENV LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64"
+ENV CPATH=$HIP_INCLUDE_PATH
+ENV PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$ROCM_PATH/lib/pkgconfig"
+
+# TE 2.17 + jax segfault fix: blank LD_LIBRARY_PATH for the shipped runtime.
+# The rocm-sdk-devel lib dirs put on LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the jax_base stage are
+# needed at build time (hipcc / RCCL / UCX / OpenMPI must find ROCm), but at
+# runtime they shadow the ROCm libs that transformer_engine_rocm_jax and
+# jax_rocm7_plugin bundle and reference via their wheel RPATH. That loads two
+# mismatched copies of the HIP/ROCm runtime, and the CK-JIT fmha_bwd kernel
+# dlopen segfaults inside the first pjit step on gfx950. Clearing it here --
+# after every build step -- lets each wheel resolve ROCm through its own RPATH.
+# The in-place RCCL override in jax_base does not depend on LD_LIBRARY_PATH, so
+# it is unaffected.
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=""
+
+# JAX
+# Note: JAX and related libraries need to be installed before TE
+ARG JAX_VERSION=0.12.0
+ENV JAX_VERSION=${JAX_VERSION}
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/jax/whl-next/jax-rocm10-pjrt/
+ENV JAX_PJRT_VERSION=0.12.0+rocm10.3.0a20261026
+# See: https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/jax/whl-next/jax-rocm10-plugin/
+ENV JAX_PLUGIN_VERSION=0.12.0+rocm10.3.0a20261026
+
+RUN uv pip install jax==${JAX_VERSION} jaxlib==${JAX_VERSION} scipy==1.16 \
+    && uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/jax/whl-next/ \
+        --pre \
+        jax_rocm10_pjrt==${JAX_PJRT_VERSION} \
+        jax_rocm10_plugin==${JAX_PLUGIN_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# TransformerEngine
+# See: https://rocm.frameworks-nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch-staging/transformer-engine-rocm-jax/
+ARG TE_VERSION=2.19.0.dev0+rocm10.2.0a20261002.bfe94fb
+
+# flaxlib_src (bundled inside the flax wheel) is inert vendored Rust/C++ reference
+# source: flax only imports the compiled flaxlib extension when flax_use_flaxlib is
+# enabled (default off), and no such extension is ever built here, so it's unreachable
+# either way. Delete it below to drop its Cargo.lock (stale pyo3 CVE) with no behavior
+# change. This pin/deletion is repeated again after the Primus install further down,
+# since Primus transitively pulls in a newer flax that reintroduces flaxlib_src.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        pybind11==3.0.4 \
+        importlib-metadata==8.7.1 \
+        pydantic==2.13.4 \
+        flax==0.12.10 \
+    && uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://rocm.frameworks-nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch-staging/ \
+        --pre \
+        --no-build-isolation \
+        transformer_engine_rocm_jax==${TE_VERSION} \
+        transformer-engine-rocm10==${TE_VERSION} \
+    && sed -i 's|transformer-engine-rocm7|transformer-engine-rocm7", "transformer-engine-rocm10|g' \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformer_engine/common/__init__.py \
+    && find /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/orbax -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && rm -rf /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flaxlib_src \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+COPY --from=gcsfuse_builder /mount.gcsfuse /usr/sbin/mount.gcsfuse
+
+FROM jax_base AS jax_training
+
+# Intentionally root (no USER instruction): training entrypoints need direct
+# access to /dev/kfd and /dev/dri GPU device nodes and to AINIC/RDMA devices,
+# which a non-root user cannot reliably get across the container runtimes this
+# image is deployed on. Trivy DS-0002 is expected to keep flagging this;
+# tracked as an accepted risk rather than remediated here.
+
+# Configure required envs
+ENV NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=1
+ENV NVTE_USE_HIPBLASLT=1
+ENV GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2
+ENV HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+ENV HSA_FORCE_FINE_GRAIN_PCIE=1
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
+ENV NCCL_DEBUG=VERSION
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_BWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_FWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_IS_V3_ATOMIC_FP32=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_HOW_V3_BF16_CVT=2
+ENV XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=.9
+ENV XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor=95 --xla_gpu_reduce_scatter_combine_threshold_bytes=8589934592 --xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler=True --xla_gpu_all_gather_combine_threshold_bytes=8589934592 --xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=False --xla_gpu_enable_cublaslt=True --xla_gpu_autotune_level=0 --xla_gpu_enable_all_gather_combine_by_dim=FALSE --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=''"
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Install maxtext
+ARG MAXTEXT_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/maxtext.git
+ARG MAXTEXT_BRANCH=release/v26.9
+
+RUN git clone ${MAXTEXT_REPO} \
+    && cd maxtext \
+    && git checkout ${MAXTEXT_BRANCH} \
+    && chmod +x src/dependencies/scripts/setup.sh \
+    && ./src/dependencies/scripts/setup.sh TF=true \
+    && cd .. \
+    && find maxtext -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Make the clone above the one MaxText-consuming tools resolve to. Primus picks its
+# MaxText backend from MAXTEXT_PATH and otherwise falls back to its own
+# third_party/maxtext submodule, which pins whatever release Primus/main tracks
+# rather than MAXTEXT_BRANCH -- so without this a run silently tests the wrong
+# MaxText. Set as ENV (not just in the CI scripts) so every entrypoint in the image
+# inherits it. Primus's own bare-metal installer exports the same var for this reason
+# (Primus tools/installation-jax/env.sh).
+ENV MAXTEXT_PATH=/workspace/maxtext
+
+# Fix (root cause): the prebuilt PyPI TensorFlow wheel bundles an LLVM whose symbols
+# collide with ROCm 7.14's libLLVM inside Grain "spawn" workers -> SIGSEGV on
+# `import tensorflow` after `import jax`. Rebuild the CPU-only TF wheel from ROCm's
+# fork (correct symbol visibility) and install it in place of the stock wheel. A CPU
+# build also has no bundled NCCL, so it preserves the previous XLA-RCCL fix.
+# NOTE: bumps TF to 2.21.0 and adds a long (~30-60 min) bazel build to the image.
+# bazel is already installed via the bazelisk_builder stage above (jax_base ->
+# jax_training inherits /usr/local/bin/bazel) -- reused here rather than
+# re-downloading the vulnerable prebuilt bazelisk release.
+ARG TF_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/tensorflow-upstream.git
+ARG TF_BRANCH=upstream-v2.21.0
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip zip \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+# GitHub's on-the-fly gzip for the pinned LLVM archive has an unstable checksum that breaks
+# the TF build. Pull a frozen copy from our ACR and feed Bazel via --distdir (no network fetch).
+COPY --from=unifiedtrainingdockers.azurecr.io/utd/mirror:llvm-909041e4802c4b9a2223ca04099f35bf1dbbd460 \
+    /909041e4802c4b9a2223ca04099f35bf1dbbd460.tar.gz /opt/bazel_distdir/
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${TF_BRANCH} ${TF_REPO} tensorflow-upstream \
+    && cd tensorflow-upstream \
+    && grep -q 3f986184ee126677dbd77edb16d6b82c057ec869fefd7a9871979941e52e837a \
+        third_party/xla/third_party/llvm/workspace.bzl \
+    && bazel build //tensorflow/tools/pip_package:wheel \
+        --distdir=/opt/bazel_distdir \
+        --repo_env=WHEEL_NAME=tensorflow_cpu \
+        --repo_env=HERMETIC_PYTHON_VERSION=3.12 \
+    && uv pip uninstall tensorflow tensorflow-cpu tensorflow_cpu \
+    && uv pip install --no-deps \
+        bazel-bin/tensorflow/tools/pip_package/wheel_house/tensorflow_cpu-2.21.0-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf tensorflow-upstream /root/.cache/bazel /root/.cache /opt/bazel_distdir
+
+# Primus
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus.git
+# Latest commit on `release/v26.9` branch. Commited on 2026-10-30.
+ARG PRIMUS_BRANCH=db1a41601833294231daadb3cdbb2933eb805c73
+
+RUN git clone --recurse-submodules ${PRIMUS_REPO} \

 ---
 
-## Highlights for v26.8
+## Highlights for v26.9
 
-**The two families split on ROCm.** `rocm/primus` moves to the ROCm 10.1.0 release with PyTorch 2.14, and builds Transformer Engine and Flash Attention from source again. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20260923`) with JAX 0.11.1 and a Transformer Engine 2.18 development build, and **no longer ships a copy of Primus**: run it with a `release/v26.8` checkout, which `primus-cli container` mounts for you. Bare-metal installs changed accordingly — see [Bare-metal installation](./bare-metal-installation.md) and the [JAX guide](./bare-metal-installation-jax.md).
+**Both families move to ROCm nightlies.** `rocm/primus` moves from the ROCm 10.1.0 release to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20261020`), with a PyTorch 2.16 pre-release and a Transformer Engine 2.20 development build, still built from source. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.3 nightly (`10.3.0a20261026`) with JAX 0.12.0, a Transformer Engine 2.19 development build, and MaxText `release/v26.9`, and **ships a copy of Primus again**. Both images were built from the same Primus commit, `db1a4160` on `release/v26.9`—see [Primus source for v26.9](#primus-source-for-v269).
 
 ### Both families
 
+- **A convergence test for Megatron and MaxText.** `tools/convergence_test/` builds a dataset from a real corpus, lints the config for settings that silently spoil a convergence run (mock or synthetic data, forced load balancing, vocab mismatches), trains through the normal `primus-cli` path, plots the loss, and gates it against a previous release's baseline ([#1229](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1229)). It ships Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-2-7B, and Mixtral-8x7B recipes for both backends, plus a MaxText Llama-2-7B FP8 recipe for MI355X ([#1261](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1261)).
+- **The `tools/perf` batch runner is ready for unattended runs.** Each run is bounded by `MAX_RUN_SECONDS` (default 1 h) and `MAX_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 20 min); busy GPUs and bad network interfaces are refused up front; failures are classified with the log line that shows them; every result records the image, host, and platform it came from; diffusion and DLRM benchmarks join the batch; and results go into an Excel report that can compare against a baseline ([#1260](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1260), [#1266](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1266), [#1299](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1299)). Two misreported throughput values are fixed: TorchTitan values printed with a thousands separator, and Megatron-Bridge's post-training estimate. Note the behavior changes: single-node runs now time out, output files have fixed names, and the runners exit non-zero when any run fails.
+- **Release benchmark suites in the auto-benchmark menu.** One choice detects the GPU and runs the whole Primus suite (Megatron, Megatron Bridge, TorchTitan) or JAX suite (MaxText, MaxDiffusion), recording the image digest, Primus commit, and submodule pins with every result ([#1251](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1251)).
+- **A preset `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is kept.** The runner used to overwrite it with `0..GPUS_PER_NODE-1`, so on a shared node a job could land on another user's GPU; it now keeps your selection and warns when its count differs from `GPUS_PER_NODE` ([#1237](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1237)).
+
+### `rocm/primus`: Megatron-LM and TorchTitan
+
+#### Changes you might need to act on
+
+- **Mock-data runs use the model's real vocabulary.** Megatron mock data used to size every model for a 131,072-token vocabulary; each model config now sets its real `vocab_size`, so embeddings, output layer, and logits have their true size. Mock-data throughput and memory are therefore not comparable with earlier releases ([#1249](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1249)).
+- **Megatron-only example material moved under `examples/megatron/`.** For example `examples/deepseek-v4/` is now `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/`, and `examples/moe_package/` is now `examples/megatron/guides/moe_package/`; `examples/mlperf/` and `examples/hardware_configs/` stay where they were. Update scripts that name the old paths ([#1130](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1130)).
+- **Some environment switches are now config keys, and the old variables do nothing.** `PRIMUS_FUSED_QK_RMSNORM_ROPE` is replaced by `use_turbo_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope` ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)); `PRIMUS_TURBO_CROSS_ENTROPY` and `PRIMUS_TURBO_CE_OVERWRITE_INPUT` by `use_turbo_cross_entropy` and `turbo_ce_overwrite_input` ([#1245](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1245)); the MoE gather-quantization variables by `moe_permute_quant_fusion`, `moe_backward_permute_quant_fusion`, and `moe_skip_identity_sort` ([#1241](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1241)).
+- **Transformer Engine fused cross entropy reuses the logits buffer by default** (`te_ce_overwrite_input: true`), so after the loss backward the logits tensor holds its gradient. Set it to `false` when the same logits feed anything else in the step, such as a distillation or auxiliary loss, metrics, or hooks ([#1287](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1287)).
+- **TorchTitan uses a Triton fused AdamW by default** (`optimizer.use_triton_fused_adam: true`). Checkpoints stay interchangeable with `torch.optim.AdamW`; set the flag to `false` to go back to it. Reading `optimizer.state` directly between steps now shows stale `step` values ([#1233](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1233)).
+- **Turbo grouped GEMM expects expandable segments.** Primus warns when `use_turbo_grouped_gemm` is on without `expandable_segments:True`, and a runner hook stops the launch when `expandable_segments:True` is requested but not in effect on the PyTorch build ([#1257](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1257)).
+
+#### New features
+
+- **GLM-5.3-Flash** (`model_type: glm5_next`): KDA linear attention, DSA sparse attention, and manifold-constrained hyper-connections with a 288-expert MoE, an MI355X BF16 recipe, and online loading of the released Hugging Face checkpoint for any TP / EP / PP layout ([#1230](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1230)). Packed sequences now run under context parallelism ([#1265](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1265)) and text-only checkpoint exports load ([#1254](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1254)). Training was validated on an 8-layer proxy; the full 45-layer model was checked forward-only against SGLang, and its DSA indexer is frozen.
+- **ZAYA1-8B FP8 recipes** for MI300X, MI325X, and MI355X (`fp8: hybrid`, tensorwise scaling, accurate from a cold start) and an MI325X BF16 recipe ([#1269](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1269)); the MI355X micro-batch sizes now fill that GPU's memory ([#1279](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1279)).
+- **HunyuanWorld-Mirror post-training**, stage 1 (geometry heads) and stage 2 (Gaussian head), with MI355X configs launched through `train posttrain`. The upstream trainer is the new `third_party/HunyuanWorld-Mirror-rocm` submodule; Primus applies ROCm fixes at runtime ([#1242](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1242)).
+- **MiniMax-M3 on MegaMoE.** The fused MegaMoE expert layer accepts MiniMax-M3's `swigluoai` activation and matches the DeepEP path's loss ([#1243](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1243)).
+- **Opt-in fusions:** Primus-Turbo fused cross entropy for TP1 training ([#1245](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1245)); FlyDSL Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE and residual RMSNorm + MXFP4 QKV fusions for GPT-OSS ([#1208](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1208)), with the fused Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE now also covering head dimension 128 ([#1247](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1247)); and gradient reduce-scatter on the GPU's copy engines (`MEGATRON_GRAD_REDUCE_BACKEND=rccl_sdma`, which needs an RCCL build with CE ReduceScatter) ([#1207](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1207)).
+- **MI455X FP8 hybrid LoRA SFT proxies** for Llama-2-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, and Qwen3-235B-A22B on one GPU ([#1248](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1248)).
